title.en: Volume 166 Biographies 116: Yuan Zhen, Bai Juyi
title.raw: 卷一百六十六 列傳第一百十六: 元稹 白居易 Volume 166 Biographies 116: Yuan Zhen, Bai Juyi

sentences.zh: 裴度，字中立，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Du, styled Zhongli, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, whose courtesy name was Zhongli, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖有鄰，濮州濮陽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Youlin was magistrate of Puyang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Youlin had served as magistrate of Puyang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 父漵，河南府澠池丞。

translations.literal: His father Yin was vice-prefect of Chi in Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had been vice-prefect of Chi in the Henan prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 度，貞元五年進士擢第，登宏辭科。

translations.literal: Du, in the fifth year of Zhenyuan, was selected in the jinshi examination and passed the Hongci examination.
translations.idiomatic: Du passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Zhenyuan reign and also qualified in the Hongci literary examination.

sentences.zh: 應制舉賢良方正、能直言極諫科，對策高等，授河陰縣尉。

translations.literal: He responded to the imperial summons for the examination of worthy and upright men and those able to speak bluntly with utmost remonstrance, ranked high in the policy answers, and was appointed county assistant of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the special imperial examination for worthy and upright men and for candid critics, placed high in the policy responses, and was appointed assistant magistrate of Heyin county.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，密疏論權幸，語切忤旨，出為河南府功曹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating censor; in a secret memorial he discussed powerful favorites, his words sharp and contrary to the imperial will, and he was sent out as recorder of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to investigating censor, he submitted a secret memorial attacking powerful favorites in language so sharp that it offended the throne, and he was transferred out to serve as recorder of Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant of the diaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed attendant of the imperial diaries.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，以司封員外郎知制誥，尋轉本司郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, as assistant director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments he was charged with drafting edicts; soon he was transferred to director within the same bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he drafted imperial edicts as assistant director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments and was soon promoted to director within that bureau.

sentences.zh: 七年，魏博節度使田季安卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Tian Ji'an, military commissioner of Weibo, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Tian Ji'an, the military commissioner of Weibo, died.

sentences.zh: 其子懷諫幼年不任軍政，牙軍立小將田興為留後。

translations.literal: His son Huaijian was young and unfit for military and civil affairs; the commander's guard installed the junior officer Tian Xing as interim commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijian, his son, was still a boy and unfit to handle military affairs, so the commander's guard installed the junior officer Tian Xing as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 興布心腹於朝廷，請守國法，除吏輸常賦，憲宗遣度使魏州宣諭。

translations.literal: Xing placed trusted men in the court, requested to observe state law, appoint officials, and pay regular tribute; Emperor Xianzong sent Du to Weizhou to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Xing placed trusted agents at court, asked to abide by imperial law, accept centrally appointed officials, and pay regular tribute, whereupon Emperor Xianzong sent Du to Weizhou as imperial envoy to announce the court's will.

sentences.zh: 興承僭侈之後，車服垣屋，有逾制度，視事齋閣，尤加宏敞。

translations.literal: Xing, inheriting the era of usurpation and extravagance, had carriages, robes, walls, and houses exceeding regulations; the hall where he conducted affairs was especially vast and spacious.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the extravagant ways of his predecessors' semi-independent rule, Xing maintained carriages, dress, walls, and halls that exceeded proper regulations, and the office pavilion where he conducted business was especially grand.

sentences.zh: 興惡之，不於其間視事，乃除舊采訪使廳居之，請度為壁記，述興謙降奉法，魏人深德之。

translations.literal: Xing disliked it and did not conduct affairs there; he cleared the old visiting commissioner hall to live in and asked Du to compose a wall inscription describing Xing's humility, submission, and observance of law; the people of Wei deeply esteemed this.
translations.idiomatic: Xing disliked the display and refused to conduct business there, moving instead into the old visiting commissioner hall and asking Du to compose an inscription for the wall praising his humility and obedience to law; the people of Wei were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 興又請度遍至屬郡，宣述詔旨，魏人郊迎感悅。

translations.literal: Xing also asked Du to go throughout the subordinate prefectures, proclaiming and explaining the edict; the people of Wei met him in the suburbs with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Xing also asked Du to tour the subordinate prefectures and proclaim the imperial edicts, and the people of Wei welcomed him in the suburbs with delight.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the mission he was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year, he was changed to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year he was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宣徽院五坊小使，每歲秋按鷹犬於畿甸，所至官吏必厚邀供餉，小不如意，即恣其須索，百姓畏之如寇盜。

translations.literal: The junior commissioners of the Five Wards of the Xuanhui Court each autumn hunted with hawks and dogs in the capital region; wherever they went, officials had to lavishly entertain and supply them, and if slightly displeased they indulged every demand; the common people feared them like bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn the junior commissioners of the Five Wards of the Xuanhui Court ranged through the capital region with hawks and hunting dogs, and wherever they went local officials had to lavish entertainment and supplies upon them; the slightest dissatisfaction provoked extortionate demands, and common people feared them like robbers.

sentences.zh: 先是，貞元末，此輩暴橫尤甚，乃至張網羅於民家門及井，不令出入汲水，曰：「驚我供奉鳥雀。」

translations.literal: Previously, at the end of Zhenyuan, this sort were especially violent and overbearing, even stretching nets at common people's gates and wells, not allowing them to go in or out to draw water, saying: 'You will startle my tribute birds.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Zhenyuan reign, they had been even more brutal, stretching nets across commoners' gates and wells and forbidding anyone to draw water, saying, 'You will frighten the birds I keep for imperial tribute.'

sentences.zh: 又群聚於賣酒食家，肆情飲啖。

translations.literal: They also gathered in groups at shops selling wine and food, indulging freely in eating and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: They also gathered in taverns and food shops and ate and drank as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 將去，留蛇一篋，誡之曰：「吾以此蛇致供奉鳥雀，可善飼之，無使饑渴。」

translations.literal: When about to leave, they would leave a basket with a snake, admonishing them: 'I use this snake to catch tribute birds; you must feed it well and not let it hunger or thirst.'
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to leave, they would leave behind a basket containing a snake with the warning, 'I use this snake to catch the birds for imperial tribute. Feed it well and do not let it go hungry or thirsty.'

sentences.zh: 主人賂而謝之，方肯攜蛇篋而去。

translations.literal: The host would bribe them and apologize before they would consent to take the snake basket away.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the proprietor paid them off and apologized would they agree to take the snake basket away.

sentences.zh: 至元和初，雖數治其弊，故態未絕。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Yuanhe, although their abuses were several times corrected, the old behavior had not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of the Yuanhe reign, although the court had repeatedly tried to curb these abuses, the old conduct had not disappeared.

sentences.zh: 小使嘗至下邽縣，縣令裴寰性嚴刻，嫉其兇暴，公館之外，一無曲奉。

translations.literal: A junior commissioner once came to Xia Gui county; the magistrate Pei Huan was stern by nature, detested their violence, and beyond the official lodge gave them no special favors.
translations.idiomatic: Once a junior commissioner came to Xia Gui county, where Magistrate Pei Huan, a stern man who detested their brutality, refused to offer them any favors beyond what the official lodge required.

sentences.zh: 小使怒，構寰出慢言。

translations.literal: The junior commissioner was angry and fabricated that Huan had spoken disrespectfully.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner grew angry and fabricated a charge that Huan had spoken disrespectfully.

sentences.zh: 及上聞，憲宗怒，促令攝寰下獄，欲以大不敬論。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the emperor, Xianzong was angry and urgently ordered Huan seized and imprisoned, intending to charge him with grave disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Xianzong was furious and ordered Huan seized and thrown into prison, intending to prosecute him for grave disrespect.

sentences.zh: 宰相武元衡等以理開悟，帝怒不解。

translations.literal: The chief ministers Wu Yuanheng and others tried to enlighten him with reason, but the emperor's anger was not dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng and others tried to reason with him, but the emperor's anger did not subside.

sentences.zh: 度入延英奏事，因極言論列，言寰無罪。

translations.literal: Du entered the Yanying Hall to report on affairs and thereupon spoke at length in argument, saying Huan was without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Du entered the Yanying Hall to report on affairs and argued at length that Huan was innocent.

sentences.zh: 上愈怒曰：「如卿之言，寰無罪即決五坊小使；

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and said: 'According to your words, if Huan is without guilt then execute the Five Wards junior commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier and said, 'If what you say is true and Huan is innocent, then execute the Five Wards commissioner;

sentences.zh: 如小使無罪，即決裴寰。」

translations.literal: if the junior commissioner is without guilt, then execute Pei Huan.'
translations.idiomatic: if the commissioner is innocent, then execute Pei Huan."

sentences.zh: 度對曰：「按罪誠如聖旨，但以裴寰為令長，憂惜陛下百姓如此，豈可加罪？」

translations.literal: Du replied: 'Judging guilt is indeed as Your Majesty says, but Pei Huan as magistrate was so concerned for Your Majesty's common people—how can guilt be added?'
translations.idiomatic: Du replied, 'Your Majesty is right that guilt must be judged, but as magistrate Pei Huan showed such concern for Your Majesty's people—how can he be punished for that?'

sentences.zh: 上怒色遽霽。

translations.literal: The emperor's angry expression quickly cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's angry expression cleared at once.

sentences.zh: 翌日，令釋寰。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered Huan released.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered Huan released.

sentences.zh: 尋以度兼刑部侍郎，奉使蔡州行營，宣諭諸軍。

translations.literal: Soon Du was additionally appointed vice minister of justice and sent on mission to the Cai prefecture field headquarters to proclaim and instruct the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Du was additionally appointed vice minister of justice and sent to the field headquarters at Cai prefecture to proclaim the court's will to the armies.

sentences.zh: 既還，帝問諸將之才，度曰：「臣觀李光顏見義能勇，終有所成。」

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor asked about the generals' abilities; Du said: 'Your servant observes that Li Guangyan, seeing righteousness, can be brave—he will ultimately achieve something.'
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor asked about the abilities of the generals. Du said, 'In my view Li Guangyan acts bravely when justice demands it and will ultimately achieve great things.'

sentences.zh: 不數日，光顏奏大破賊軍於時曲，帝尤嘆度之知人。

translations.literal: Within a few days Guangyan reported a great defeat of the rebel army at Shiqu; the emperor especially praised Du's knowledge of men.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days Guangyan reported a great victory over the rebel army at Shiqu, and the emperor especially marveled at Du's judgment of character.

sentences.zh: 十年六月，王承宗、李師道俱遣刺客刺宰相武元衡，亦令刺度。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year, Wang Chengzong and Li Shidao both sent assassins to stab Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng, and also ordered Du stabbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year, Wang Chengzong and Li Shidao each sent assassins to kill Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng and also ordered an attempt on Du's life.

sentences.zh: 是日，度出通化裏，盜三以劍擊度，初斷靴帶，次中背，才絕單衣，後微傷其首，度墮馬。

translations.literal: That day, as Du left Tonghua Lane, three bandits struck Du with swords; first they cut his boot strap, next struck his back, barely piercing his inner garment, then slightly wounded his head; Du fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: That day, as Du was leaving Tonghua Lane, three assassins attacked him with swords, first cutting his boot strap, then striking his back so that the blade barely pierced his inner garment, then slightly wounding his head, and Du fell from his horse.

sentences.zh: 會度帶氈帽，故創不至深。

translations.literal: As it happened Du wore a felt hat, so the wound did not go deep.
translations.idiomatic: Because Du was wearing a felt hat, the wound was not deep.

sentences.zh: 賊又揮刃追度，度從人王義乃持賊連呼甚急，賊反刃斷義手，乃得去。

translations.literal: The assassins again swung blades pursuing Du; Du's attendant Wang Yi then seized an assassin and shouted urgently; the assassin turned his blade and cut off Yi's hand, and only then got away.
translations.idiomatic: The assassins pursued Du with drawn blades, but his attendant Wang Yi seized one of them and shouted for help; the assassin turned and cut off Yi's hand before escaping.

sentences.zh: 度已墮溝中，賊謂度已死，乃舍去。

translations.literal: Du had already fallen into a ditch; the assassins thought Du was dead and so left him.
translations.idiomatic: Du had fallen into a ditch, and the assassins, believing him dead, abandoned the attack.

sentences.zh: 居三日，詔以度為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Within three days an edict appointed Du as vice minister of the Secretariat and participant in the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later an edict appointed Du vice minister of the Secretariat and participant in the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 度勁正而言辯，尤長於政體，凡所陳諭，感動物情。

translations.literal: Du was firm and upright and eloquent in speech, especially skilled in governmental institutions; whatever he presented and explained moved people's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Du was upright, forceful, and eloquent, especially skilled in matters of statecraft, and whatever he presented moved those who heard him.

sentences.zh: 自魏博使還，宣達稱旨，帝深嘉屬。

translations.literal: From the time he returned from the Weibo mission, his proclamations accorded with the imperial will, and the emperor deeply praised and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: From his return from the Weibo mission onward, his proclamations pleased the emperor, who came to rely on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 又自蔡州勞軍還，益聽其言。

translations.literal: Again, from his return after comforting the armies at Cai, the emperor increasingly heeded his words.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned from comforting the armies at Cai, the emperor listened to him even more closely.

sentences.zh: 尚以元衡秉政，大用未果，自盜發都邑，便以大計屬之。

translations.literal: While Yuanheng still held power, great employment had not yet been realized; from the time bandits struck the capital, the great plan was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanheng still dominated the government, Du had not yet received full authority, but once assassins struck in the capital the emperor entrusted the great undertaking to him.

sentences.zh: 初，元衡遇害，獻計者或請罷度官以安二鎮之心，憲宗大怒曰：「若罷度官，是奸計得行，朝綱何以振舉？

translations.literal: At first, when Yuanheng met disaster, some who offered plans requested that Du's office be abolished to reassure the hearts of the two circuits; Xianzong was greatly angry and said: 'If Du's office is abolished, the traitors' scheme succeeds—how can court discipline be upheld?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanheng was killed, some advisers suggested removing Du from office to placate the two rebellious circuits, but Xianzong was furious and said, 'If I remove Du from office, the traitors' plot succeeds. How then can court authority be upheld?

sentences.zh: 吾用度一人，足以破此二賊矣。」

translations.literal: Using Du alone, I am sufficient to break these two bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: With Du alone I am enough to destroy these two rebels."

sentences.zh: 度亦以平賊為己任。

translations.literal: Du also took pacifying the bandits as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Du likewise took the suppression of the rebels as his personal duty.

sentences.zh: 度以所傷請告二十余日，詔以衛兵宿度私第，中使問訊不絕。

translations.literal: Du requested leave for his wounds for more than twenty days; an edict ordered guards to lodge at Du's private residence, and palace envoys inquired without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Du requested more than twenty days' leave for his wounds, and the court ordered imperial guards to lodge at his residence while palace envoys inquired after him without pause.

sentences.zh: 未拜前一日，宣旨謂度曰：「不用宣政參假，即延英對來。」

translations.literal: On the day before his appointment, an imperial message told Du: 'Do not take leave to attend at Xuanzheng; come directly to audience in the Yanying Hall.'
translations.idiomatic: On the day before his formal appointment, the emperor sent word telling Du, 'Do not request leave to attend at Xuanzheng Hall; come straight to audience in the Yanying Hall.'

sentences.zh: 及度入對，撫諭周至。

translations.literal: When Du entered for audience, the emperor comforted and instructed him with complete care.
translations.idiomatic: When Du entered for audience, the emperor comforted and encouraged him with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 時群盜幹紀，變起都城，朝野恐駭。

translations.literal: At that time bandits violated discipline; upheaval arose in the capital; court and countryside were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: At that time rebels were violating law and disorder had erupted in the capital, filling court and countryside with fear.

sentences.zh: 及度命相制下，人情始安，以為必能殄寇。

translations.literal: When the edict appointing Du as chief minister was issued, people's hearts first settled, believing he would surely be able to exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict appointing Du chief minister was issued, public anxiety eased, for people believed he would surely destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 自是誅賊之計，日聞獻替，用軍愈急。

translations.literal: From then on plans to execute the bandits were daily heard in deliberation and revision, and military employment grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on plans for suppressing the rebels were revised daily in council, and military operations grew steadily more intense.

sentences.zh: 十一年，莊憲皇后崩，度為禮儀使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Empress Zhuangxian died; Du served as commissioner of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, after the death of Empress Zhuangxian, Du was appointed commissioner of funeral ritual.

sentences.zh: 上不聽政，欲準故事置冢宰，以總百司。

translations.literal: The emperor did not attend to government and wished, according to precedent, to establish a chief steward to oversee all offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended government and wished, following precedent, to appoint a chief steward to oversee all offices.

sentences.zh: 度獻議曰：「冢宰是殷、周六官之首，既掌邦理，實統百司。

translations.literal: Du submitted a proposal saying: 'The chief steward was head of the six ministries in Yin and Zhou, both governing the state and truly overseeing all offices.
translations.idiomatic: Du submitted a memorial arguing, 'The chief steward was head of the six ministries in the Yin and Zhou dynasties, governing the state and overseeing all offices.

sentences.zh: 故王者諒闇，百官有權聽之制。

translations.literal: Therefore when kings observed mourning seclusion, the hundred officials had the system of provisional authority to hear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler observed mourning seclusion, the hundred officials were therefore empowered to conduct government in his stead.

sentences.zh: 後代設官，既無此號，不可虛設。

translations.literal: Later ages established offices but no longer had this title; it cannot be established in empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties no longer had such an office, and it should not be created in name only.

sentences.zh: 且國朝故事，或置或否，古今異制，不必因循。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in our dynasty's precedents it was sometimes established and sometimes not; ancient and modern systems differ, and one need not follow precedent blindly.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our own dynasty had sometimes used the office and sometimes not; ancient and modern institutions differ, and precedent need not be followed blindly."

sentences.zh: 敕旨曰：「諸司公事，宜權取中書門下處分。」

translations.literal: An imperial order said: 'The public business of all offices should provisionally be handled by the Secretariat and Chancellery.'
translations.idiomatic: The imperial response ordered, "Public business of all offices should provisionally be handled by the Secretariat and Chancellery."

sentences.zh: 識者是之。

translations.literal: The knowledgeable approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledgeable officials approved of this decision.

sentences.zh: 六月，蔡州行營唐鄧節度使高霞寓兵敗於鐵城，中外恟駭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Gao Xiayu, military commissioner of Tang and Deng in the Cai prefecture field camp, was defeated at Iron City; inside and outside the court were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Gao Xiayu, military commissioner of Tang and Deng in the Cai field army, was defeated at Iron City, throwing court and countryside into alarm.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔群臣各獻誅吳元濟可否之狀。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict had ordered all ministers each to submit views on whether Wu Yuanji could be executed or not.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ordered all ministers to submit opinions on whether Wu Yuanji should be punished or pardoned.

sentences.zh: 朝臣多言罷兵赦罪為便，翰林學士錢徽、蕭俛語尤切，唯度言賊不可赦。

translations.literal: Many court officials said ceasing troops and pardoning crimes would be expedient; Hanlin academicians Qian Hui and Xiao Fu spoke especially urgently; only Du said the bandit could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Most court officials argued that ceasing military operations and granting amnesty would be best; Hanlin academicians Qian Hui and Xiao Fu spoke especially forcefully, but only Du insisted that the rebel could not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 及霞寓敗，宰相以上必厭兵，欲以罷兵為對。

translations.literal: When Xiayu was defeated, the chief ministers thought the emperor must be weary of war and intended to respond with ceasing troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiayu's defeat the chief ministers assumed the emperor must be weary of war and prepared to advise halting the campaign.

sentences.zh: 延英方奏，憲宗曰：「夫一勝一負，兵家常勢。

translations.literal: As they were reporting in the Yanying Hall, Xianzong said: 'One victory and one defeat are the constant pattern of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: As they were presenting their views in the Yanying Hall, Xianzong said, 'Victory and defeat are the ordinary pattern of war.

sentences.zh: 若帝王之兵不合敗，則自古何難於用兵，累聖不應留此兇賊。

translations.literal: If an emperor's army should not suffer defeat, then from antiquity why would warfare be difficult, and successive sage emperors should not have left this vicious bandit.
translations.idiomatic: If an imperial army were never allowed to suffer defeat, warfare would have been easy throughout history and no sage emperor would ever have tolerated such a vicious rebel.

sentences.zh: 今但論此兵合用與否，及朝廷制置當否，卿等唯須要害處置。

translations.literal: Now discuss only whether this army should be employed or not, and whether the court's arrangements are correct; you need only dispose of essential points.
translations.idiomatic: Discuss only whether this campaign should continue and whether the court's arrangements are sound. You need only advise me on the essential measures.

sentences.zh: 將帥有不可者，去之勿疑；

translations.literal: If any commander is unfit, remove him without hesitation;
translations.idiomatic: If any commander proves unfit, remove him without hesitation;

sentences.zh: 兵力有不足者，速與應接。

translations.literal: if forces are insufficient, quickly provide reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: if forces are insufficient, reinforce them at once.

sentences.zh: 何可以一將不利，便沮成計？」

translations.literal: How can one general's setback frustrate a completed plan?'
translations.idiomatic: How can a single general's setback be allowed to wreck a settled plan?"

sentences.zh: 於是宰臣不得措言，朝廷無敢言罷兵者，故度計得行。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers could find no words; in the court none dared speak of ceasing troops, and therefore Du's plan was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were left speechless, and no one at court dared propose halting the campaign, so Du's policy prevailed.

sentences.zh: 王稷家二奴告稷換父遺表，隱沒進奉物。

translations.literal: Two slaves of Wang Ji's household reported that Ji had altered his father's death memorial and concealed tribute goods presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Two slaves in Wang Ji's household reported that Ji had altered his father's death memorial and concealed goods presented as imperial tribute.

sentences.zh: 留其奴於仗內，遣中使往東都檢責稷之家財。

translations.literal: The slaves were detained in the guard quarters, and palace envoys were sent to the eastern capital to inspect and seize Ji's household property.
translations.idiomatic: The slaves were detained in the palace guard quarters while palace envoys were sent to the eastern capital to inspect and seize Ji's family property.

sentences.zh: 度奏曰：「王鍔身歿之後，其家進奉已多。

translations.literal: Du memorialized: 'After Wang E's death, his family has already presented much tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized, 'Since Wang E's death his family has already presented a great deal of tribute to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今因其奴告檢責其家事，臣恐天下將帥聞之，必有以家為計者。」

translations.literal: Now, because slaves reported, to inspect and seize his household affairs—your servant fears that when military commanders throughout the realm hear of this, there will certainly be those who calculate in terms of their households.'
translations.idiomatic: If we now investigate and seize his family's property because slaves have accused him, I fear that commanders throughout the realm will hear of it and begin calculating how to protect their households."

sentences.zh: 憲宗即日遣中使還，二奴付京兆府決殺。

translations.literal: Xianzong that same day sent the palace envoys back and handed the two slaves to the Jingzhao prefecture for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong that same day recalled the envoys and ordered the two slaves executed by the Jingzhao prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 十二年，李醖、李光顏屢奏破賊，然國家聚兵淮右四年，度支供餉，不勝其弊，諸將玩寇相視，未有成功，上亦病之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Li Yun and Li Guangyan repeatedly reported defeating bandits, yet the state had gathered troops on the Huai right for four years; the treasury supplied provisions and could not bear the harm; the generals treated the bandits lightly and watched one another, with no success achieved; the emperor also was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Li Yun and Li Guangyan repeatedly reported victories over the rebels, yet the court had kept armies on the Huai right for four years, the treasury could scarcely sustain the cost of supplies, the generals dallied with the enemy and watched one another without achieving decisive success, and the emperor himself was weary of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉、王涯等三人，以勞師弊賦，意欲罷兵，見上互陳利害。

translations.literal: The three chief ministers Li Fengji, Wang Ya, and another, because troops were weary and taxes exhausted, intended to cease military operations; seeing the emperor they each presented advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ministers Li Fengji, Wang Ya, and a third colleague, citing exhausted armies and depleted revenues, wished to halt the campaign and took turns explaining the pros and cons to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 度獨無言。

translations.literal: Du alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Du alone remained silent.

sentences.zh: 帝問之，對曰：「臣請身自督戰。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked him; he replied: 'Your servant requests to go in person to supervise the campaign.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked him, he replied, 'Your servant asks to go in person to supervise the fighting.'

sentences.zh: 明日延英重議，逢吉等出，獨留度，謂之曰：「卿必能為朕行乎？」

translations.literal: The next day in renewed deliberation in the Yanying Hall, Fengji and the others withdrew; only Du was kept, and the emperor said to him: 'Can you truly go for Us?'
translations.idiomatic: The next day, after further deliberation in the Yanying Hall, Fengji and the others withdrew and the emperor kept Du alone, asking, 'Can you truly go for me?'

sentences.zh: 度俯伏流涕曰：「臣誓不與此賊偕全。」

translations.literal: Du prostrated himself with tears flowing and said: 'Your servant vows not to survive whole together with this bandit.'
translations.idiomatic: Du prostrated himself in tears and said, 'I vow that either the rebel or I shall not survive this campaign whole.'

sentences.zh: 上亦為之改容。

translations.literal: The emperor also changed expression for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression softened at this.

sentences.zh: 度復奏曰：「臣昨見吳元濟乞降表，料此逆賊勢實窘蹙。

translations.literal: Du again memorialized: 'Your servant yesterday saw Wu Yuanji's petition to surrender; I estimate this rebellious bandit's situation is truly pressed and tight.
translations.idiomatic: Du added, 'Yesterday I saw Wu Yuanji's petition offering surrender. I judge that the rebel's position is truly desperate.

sentences.zh: 但諸將不一，未能迫之，故未降耳。

translations.literal: Only the generals are not united and cannot press him, so he has not yet surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: But the generals are not acting in concert and cannot press him, which is why he has not yet surrendered.

sentences.zh: 若臣自赴行營，則諸將各欲立功以固恩寵，破賊必矣！」

translations.literal: If your servant goes in person to the field camp, then each general will wish to achieve merit to secure favor and grace—the bandits will surely be broken!'
translations.idiomatic: If I go to the field camp in person, each general will strive to win merit and secure imperial favor, and the rebels will surely be destroyed!"

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詔曰：輔弼之臣，軍國是賴。

translations.literal: The next day an edict stated: Ministers who assist and support — on them the army and state rely.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict declared: Ministers who assist and support the throne — on them the army and state rely.

sentences.zh: 興化致理，秉鈞以居。

translations.literal: To promote transformation and achieve good order, one holds the pivot of power and dwells at the center.
translations.idiomatic: To promote transformation and good government, one holds the pivot of state and dwells at the center.

sentences.zh: 取威定功，則分閫而出。

translations.literal: To establish awe and settle achievement, one departs to take command at the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: To establish awe and settle achievement, one departs to take command in the field.

sentences.zh: 所以同君臣之體，一中外之任焉。

translations.literal: Thus the form of ruler and minister is shared, and duties inside and outside are unified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the form of ruler and minister is shared, and duties at court and in the field are unified.

sentences.zh: 屬者問罪汝南，致誅淮右，蓋欲刷其汙俗，吊彼頑人。

translations.literal: Recently We inquired into guilt at Runan and brought execution to Huai-West, intending to cleanse their corrupt customs and comfort those stubborn people.
translations.idiomatic: Recently We called Runan to account and brought punishment to Huai-West, intending to cleanse corrupt customs there and comfort those stubborn people.

sentences.zh: 雖挈地求生者實繁有徒，而嬰城執迷者未翦其類，何獸困而猶鬥，豈鳥窮之無歸歟？

translations.literal: Though those who surrendered territory to save themselves were indeed many, those who held the cities clinging to delusion had not yet had their kind cut off — why do beasts cornered still fight? Can it be that birds at the end of their path have nowhere to return?
translations.idiomatic: Though many surrendered territory to save themselves, those who held the cities in delusion had not yet been cut off — why do cornered beasts still fight? Can birds at the end of their path have nowhere to return?

sentences.zh: 由是遙聽鼓鼙，更張琴瑟，煩我臺席，董茲戎旃。

translations.literal: Therefore We listened from afar to drums and gongs, restrung lute and zither, troubled Our terrace seat, and supervised this military banner.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We listened from afar to drums and gongs, restrung lute and zither, troubled Our seat at court, and took charge of this military banner.

sentences.zh: 朝議大夫、守中書侍郎、同平章事、飛騎尉、賜紫金魚袋裴度，為時降生，協朕夢卜，精辨宣力，堅明納忠。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Court Discussion, Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, Commandant of Flying Cavalry, granted the purple-gold fish tally — Pei Du — born for the age, in accord with Our dream-divination, discerning and exerting effort, steadfast and clear in offering loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Court Discussion, Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, Commandant of Flying Cavalry, granted the purple-gold fish tally — Pei Du — born for the age, in accord with Our dream-divination, discerning and exerting himself, steadfast and clear in offering loyalty.

sentences.zh: 當軸而才謀老成，運籌而智略有定。

translations.literal: At the pivot his talent and counsel are seasoned; in plotting strategy his wisdom and plans are settled.
translations.idiomatic: At the pivot of state his talent and counsel are seasoned; in plotting strategy his wisdom and plans are settled.

sentences.zh: 司其樞務，備知四方之事；

translations.literal: He manages pivotal affairs and fully knows matters throughout the four directions;
translations.idiomatic: He manages pivotal affairs and fully knows matters throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 付以兵要，必得萬人之心。

translations.literal: Entrusted with military essentials, he is sure to win the hearts of ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with military essentials, he is sure to win the hearts of the armies.

sentences.zh: 是用禱於上玄，揀此吉日，帶丞相之印綬，所以尊其名；

translations.literal: For this We prayed to the Supreme Mystery and selected this auspicious day; girding on the chancellor's seal and sash is to honor his name;
translations.idiomatic: For this We prayed to Heaven and selected this auspicious day; girding on the chancellor's seal and sash is to honor his name;

sentences.zh: 賜諸侯之斧鉞，所以重其命。

translations.literal: bestowing upon him the feudal lord's axe and halberd is to weight his commission.
translations.idiomatic: bestowing upon him the feudal lord's axe and halberd is to weight his commission.

sentences.zh: 爾宜宣布清問，恢壯皇猷，感勵連營，蕩平多壘，招懷孤疾，字撫夷傷。

translations.literal: You should proclaim Our clear inquiry, expand and strengthen the imperial design, move and encourage the linked camps, sweep level the many fortresses, win over and embrace the orphaned and afflicted, and cherish and soothe the wounded and the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: You should proclaim Our clear inquiry, expand and strengthen the imperial design, move and encourage the linked camps, sweep level the many fortresses, win over the orphaned and afflicted, and cherish and soothe the wounded and the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 況淮西一軍，素效忠節，過海赴難，史冊書勛。

translations.literal: Moreover the Huai-West army has long rendered loyal service; crossing the sea to rush to crisis, its merit is recorded in the historical annals.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Huai-West army has long rendered loyal service; crossing the sea to rush to crisis, its merit is recorded in the historical annals.

sentences.zh: 建中初，攻破襄陽，擒滅崇義。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, it stormed Xiangyang and captured and destroyed Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign, it stormed Xiangyang and captured and destroyed Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 比者脅於兇逆，歸命無由。

translations.literal: Recently, coerced by violent rebels, they had no way to submit to Our command.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, coerced by violent rebels, they had no way to submit to Our command.

sentences.zh: 每念前勞，常思安撫。

translations.literal: Each time We recall their past labors, We always think of pacifying and comforting them.
translations.idiomatic: Each time We recall their past labors, We always think of pacifying and comforting them.

sentences.zh: 所以內輟輔臣，俾為師率，實欲保全慰諭，各使得宜。

translations.literal: Therefore We set aside an inner minister and made him their military leader, truly wishing to preserve, comfort, and instruct them so that each may obtain what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We set aside an inner minister and made him their military leader, truly wishing to preserve, comfort, and instruct them so that each may obtain what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 汝往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go — take heed!
translations.idiomatic: Go — take heed!

sentences.zh: 無越我丕訓。

translations.literal: Do not transgress Our great instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Do not transgress Our great instructions.

sentences.zh: 可門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事、蔡州刺史，充彰義軍節度、申光蔡觀察等使，仍充淮西宣慰招討處置使。

translations.literal: He is approved as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, Prefect of Caizhou, military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army and inspector of Shen, Guang, and Cai, and also commissioner for proclamation, pacification, expedition, and disposition of Huai-West.
translations.idiomatic: He is approved as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, Prefect of Caizhou, military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army and inspector of Shen, Guang, and Cai, and also commissioner for proclamation, pacification, expedition, and disposition of Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 詔出，度以韓弘為淮西行營都統，不欲更為招討，請只稱宣慰處置使。

translations.literal: After the edict was issued, because Han Hong was overall commander of the Huai west field camp, Du did not wish to be made pacification commissioner again and requested to be called only commissioner for proclamation and disposition.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was issued, since Han Hong had been appointed overall commander of the Huai west field army, Du declined the title of pacification commissioner and asked to be styled only commissioner for proclamation and disposition.

sentences.zh: 又以此行既兼招撫，請改「翦其類」為「革其誌」。

translations.literal: Also, because this mission combined both attack and appeasement, he requested changing 'cut off their kind' to 'reform their will.'
translations.idiomatic: Because the mission combined military action with appeasement, he also asked to change the phrase 'cut off their kind' to 'reform their will.'

sentences.zh: 又以弘已為都統，請改「更張琴瑟」為「近輟樞衡」，請改「煩我臺席」為「授以成算」，皆從之。

translations.literal: Also, because Hong was already overall commander, he requested changing 'restring the lute' to 'recently set aside the pivot and balance,' and changing 'trouble Our terrace seat' to 'entrust with the completed plan'—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hong was already overall commander, he asked to change 'restring the lute' to 'recently set aside the pivot of state,' and 'trouble Our terrace seat' to 'entrust with the completed plan,' and the emperor approved all these revisions.

sentences.zh: 仍奏刑部侍郎馬總為宣慰副使，太子右庶子韓愈為彰義行軍司馬，司勛員外郎李正封、都官員外郎馮宿、禮部員外郎李宗閔等為兩使判官書記，皆從之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Vice Minister of Justice Ma Zong be deputy commissioner for proclamation, Crown Prince's right assistant Han Yu be staff officer of the Zhangyi field army, and Assistant Directors Li Zhengfeng, Feng Su, and Li Zongmin of various ministries be clerks and secretaries for both commissioners—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Vice Minister of Justice Ma Zong as deputy commissioner, Crown Prince's right assistant Han Yu as staff officer of the Zhangyi field army, and Assistant Directors Li Zhengfeng, Feng Su, and Li Zongmin as secretaries for both commissioners, and all were approved.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗朝政多僻，朝官或相過從，多令金吾伺察密奏，宰相不敢於私第見賓客。

translations.literal: At first, under Dezong the court government was often perverse; when court officials visited one another, the golden guards were often ordered to spy and report secretly; chief ministers did not dare receive guests at their private residences.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Emperor Dezong the court had been suspicious of officials, and when courtiers visited one another the golden guards were often ordered to spy and report secretly, so that chief ministers did not dare receive guests at their private residences.

sentences.zh: 及度輔政，以群賊未誅，宜延接奇士，共為籌畫，乃請於私居接延賓客，憲宗許之。

translations.literal: When Du assisted in government, because the bandits had not yet been executed, it was fitting to receive extraordinary men and plan together; he therefore requested to receive and extend hospitality to guests at his private residence, and Xianzong permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Du entered government, he argued that while the rebels had not yet been destroyed it was right to receive talented men and plan with them, and he asked permission to entertain guests at his private residence, which Xianzong granted.

sentences.zh: 自是天下賢俊，得以效計議於丞相，接士於私第，由度之請也。

translations.literal: From then on worthy men throughout the realm could offer plans and counsel to the chief minister; receiving scholars at private residences began with Du's request.
translations.idiomatic: From then on talented men throughout the realm could offer counsel to the chief minister, and the custom of receiving scholars at one's private residence began with Du's request.

sentences.zh: 自討淮西，王師屢敗。

translations.literal: Since the campaign against the Huai west, the imperial armies had repeatedly been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Since the campaign against the Huai west began, the imperial armies had suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 論者以殺傷滋甚，轉輸不逮，擬議密疏，紛紜交進。

translations.literal: Critics, because casualties grew ever worse and transport could not keep up, drafted secret memorials that came in profusion one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Critics, citing ever heavier casualties and inadequate supply lines, submitted secret memorials in a steady flood of conflicting advice.

sentences.zh: 度以腹心之疾，不時去之，終為大患，不然，兩河之盜，亦將視此為高下。

translations.literal: Du regarded it as a disease of the heart and viscera; if not removed in time it would ultimately become a great calamity—otherwise the bandits of the two He rivers would also take this as their measure of high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Du regarded the rebellion as a disease of the heart and viscera that would become a grave calamity if not removed in time; otherwise the rebels of the two He regions would take their measure from this campaign as well.

sentences.zh: 遂堅請討伐，上深委信，故聽之不疑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he firmly requested a punitive campaign; the emperor deeply entrusted and believed in him, and therefore listened without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his case for a punitive campaign with unwavering resolve, and the emperor, placing deep trust in him, assented without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 度既受命，召對於延英，奏曰：「主憂臣辱，義在必死。

translations.literal: Once Du had received the commission, he was summoned for audience in the Yanying Hall and memorialized, saying: 'When the ruler is troubled, the minister is shamed; righteousness requires that one must die.
translations.idiomatic: Once Du had received his commission, he was summoned to audience in the Yanying Hall and said, "When the sovereign grieves, the minister is disgraced; duty demands that I stake my life on this mission.

sentences.zh: 賊滅，則朝天有日；

translations.literal: If the rebels are destroyed, then there will be a day to attend court;
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels are destroyed, I shall again see the imperial court;

sentences.zh: 賊在，則歸闕無期。」

translations.literal: if the rebels remain, then return to the palace will be without term.'
translations.idiomatic: but while they remain, I shall never return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 上為之惻然流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor, on his account, was deeply moved and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and wept at his words.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月三日，度赴淮西，詔以神策軍三百騎衛從，上御通化門慰勉之。

translations.literal: On the third day of the eighth month of the twelfth year, Du departed for Huai West; an edict ordered three hundred riders of the Shence Army to escort him, and the emperor went out to the Tonghua Gate to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the eighth month of the twelfth year, Du set out for Huai West. An edict assigned three hundred Shence cavalry as his escort, and the emperor himself came to the Tonghua Gate to send him off with words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 度樓下銜涕而辭，賜之犀帶。

translations.literal: Du, below the tower, took tears in his mouth and took leave; he was granted a rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: Below the gate tower Du took his leave with tears choking his voice, and the emperor bestowed on him a rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 度名雖宣慰，其實行元帥事，仍以郾城為治所。

translations.literal: Du's title was though pacification commissioner, in fact he exercised the affairs of commander-in-chief, and still took Yancheng as his seat of administration.
translations.idiomatic: Although Du's title was pacification commissioner, in practice he exercised full command, and he established his headquarters at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 上以李逢吉與度不協，乃罷知政事，出為劍南東川節度。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew Li Fengji and Du were not in accord, he removed Fengji from participation in governance and sent him out as military commissioner of Jiannan East Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Fengji and Du were at odds, the emperor removed Fengji from the chancellorship and sent him out to serve as military commissioner of Jiannan East Chuan.

sentences.zh: 既離京，淮西行營大將李光顏、烏重胤謂監軍梁守謙曰：「若俟度至而有功，即非我利。

translations.literal: Once he had left the capital, the great generals of the Huai West field camp, Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin, said to the army supervisor Liang Shouqian: 'If we wait until Du arrives and then achieve merit, that will not be to our advantage.
translations.idiomatic: After Du had left the capital, the chief generals of the Huai West field camp, Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin, told the army supervisor Liang Shouqian, "If we wait until Du arrives and then win the glory, it will do us no good.

sentences.zh: 可疾戰，先事立功。」

translations.literal: We can fight swiftly and achieve merit before the event.'
translations.idiomatic: We should strike quickly and win credit before he gets here."

sentences.zh: 是月六日，將出兵，與賊戰於賈店，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of that month they were about to move out and fought the rebels at Jia Store; they were defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of that month they took the field and fought the rebels at Jia Store, where they were routed.

sentences.zh: 度二十七日至郾城，巡撫諸軍，宣達上旨，士皆賈勇。

translations.literal: Du on the twenty-seventh day reached Yancheng, inspected and comforted the various armies, proclaimed and conveyed the emperor's intent, and the soldiers all mustered courage.
translations.idiomatic: Du reached Yancheng on the twenty-seventh. He inspected the armies, conveyed the emperor's will, and the soldiers rallied their courage.

sentences.zh: 時諸道兵皆有中使監陣，進退不由主將，戰勝則先使獻捷，偶衄則淩挫百端。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of the various circuits all had palace envoys supervising the battle lines; advance and retreat were not at the command of the chief generals. If victorious in battle the envoys first presented the victory report; if occasionally defeated they heaped humiliation in every way.
translations.idiomatic: At that time every allied army had palace envoys supervising the lines. Generals could not command advance or retreat on their own; when a battle was won the envoys rushed forward to claim the victory report, and when there was even a minor setback they heaped abuse on every side.

sentences.zh: 度至行營，並奏去之，兵柄專制之於將，眾皆喜悅。

translations.literal: When Du reached the field camp, he memorialized to remove them all; military authority was exclusively controlled by the generals, and the masses were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Du reached the field camp he memorialized to remove them all, so that military authority rested solely with the generals, to the great satisfaction of the troops.

sentences.zh: 軍法嚴肅，號令畫一，以是出戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Military law was strict and solemn, orders uniform throughout; because of this every sortie was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was strict and orders uniform, and from that point every engagement ended in victory.

sentences.zh: 度遣使入蔡州，元濟與度書曰：「比密有降款，而索日進隔河大呼，遂令三軍防元濟，故歸首無路。」

translations.literal: Du sent an envoy into Cai prefecture; Yuanji wrote to Du, saying: 'Recently I secretly had terms of surrender, but Suo Rijin shouted loudly across the river, whereupon he caused the three armies to guard against Yuanji, and therefore there was no road to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Du sent an envoy into Cai prefecture, and Wu Yuanji wrote to him, "I had lately been negotiating a secret surrender, but Suo Rijin shouted the news across the river, and the three armies were put on guard against me, so I had no way to give myself up."

sentences.zh: 十月十一日，唐鄧節度使李醖，襲破懸瓠城，擒吳元濟。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the tenth month, Li Yun, military commissioner of Tang-Deng, raided and broke Xuanhuo city and captured Wu Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the tenth month, Li Yun, military commissioner of Tang-Deng, stormed Xuanhuo city and captured Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 度先遣宣慰副使馬總入城安撫。

translations.literal: Du first sent the pacification deputy commissioner Ma Zong into the city to pacify and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: Du first sent Ma Zong, his deputy pacification commissioner, into the city to restore order and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 明日，度建彰義軍節，領洄曲降卒萬人繼進。

translations.literal: The next day Du established the Zhangyi Army command, leading ten thousand surrendered troops from Huichu to follow in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Du entered as military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army, followed by ten thousand surrendered troops from Huichu.

sentences.zh: 李愬具櫜鞬以軍禮迎度，拜之路左。

translations.literal: Li Su, equipped with bow case and quiver, welcomed Du with military ceremony and bowed at the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su came out with bow case and quiver in full military ceremony to welcome Du, bowing at the roadside.

sentences.zh: 度既視事，蔡人大悅。

translations.literal: Once Du had assumed office, the people of Cai were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Du took up his duties, the people of Cai were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 舊令：途無偶語，夜不燃燭，人或以酒食相過從者，以軍法論。

translations.literal: The old regulations: on the roads no paired speech; at night no lighting candles; if people visited one another with wine and food, they were judged by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations no one might speak in pairs on the streets, lamps were forbidden after dark, and anyone who visited a neighbor with food or wine was punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 度乃約法，唯盜賊、鬥殺外，余盡除之，其往來者，不復以晝夜為限。

translations.literal: Du thereupon simplified the law: apart from theft, banditry, and fighting-killing, the rest were all abolished; those coming and going were no longer restricted by day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Du then issued simplified regulations, abolishing every prohibition except those against theft, robbery, and murder in brawls, and people were free to come and go without regard to day or night.

sentences.zh: 於是蔡之遺黎，始知有生人之樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon the surviving common people of Cai first knew the joy of being living men.
translations.idiomatic: At last the survivors of Cai knew what it meant to live as ordinary human beings again.

sentences.zh: 初，度以蔡卒為牙兵。

translations.literal: Initially, Du made the Cai soldiers his guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: At first Du made the former Cai garrison his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 或以為反側之子，其心未安，不可自去其備。

translations.literal: Some thought that as sons of the rebellious and wavering, their hearts were not yet settled, and one could not oneself remove one's precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that these men, having once rebelled, could not yet be trusted, and that he ought not to disarm himself in their presence.

sentences.zh: 度笑而答曰：「吾受命為彰義軍節度使，元惡就擒，蔡人即吾人也。」

translations.literal: Du smiled and replied: 'I have received the commission as military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army; the chief villain has been captured, and the people of Cai are my people.'
translations.idiomatic: Du smiled and replied, "I have been appointed military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army. The chief villain is captured, and the people of Cai are my own people."

sentences.zh: 蔡之父老，無不感泣。

translations.literal: The elders of Cai, without exception, were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Cai wept at his words.

sentences.zh: 申、光之民，即時平定。

translations.literal: The people of Shen and Guang were at once pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shen and Guang were pacified at once.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十八日，度自蔡州入朝，留副使馬總為彰義軍留後。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month, Du entered court from Cai prefecture and left deputy commissioner Ma Zong as acting commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month Du returned to court from Cai prefecture, leaving Ma Zong behind as acting commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 初，度入蔡州，或譖度沒入元濟婦女珍寶。

translations.literal: Initially, when Du entered Cai prefecture, some slandered Du for confiscating Yuanji's women and precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Du entered Cai prefecture, some had accused him of seizing Wu Yuanji's women and treasures for himself.

sentences.zh: 聞，上頗疑之。

translations.literal: When he heard of it, the emperor was quite suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he grew deeply suspicious.

sentences.zh: 上欲盡誅元濟舊將，封二劍以授梁守謙，使往蔡州。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to execute all of Yuanji's old generals; he sealed two swords and entrusted them to Liang Shouqian, sending him to Cai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to execute all of Wu Yuanji's former officers and sealed two swords, which he gave to Liang Shouqian and sent him to Cai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 度回至郾城遇之，乃復與守謙入蔡州，量罪加刑，不盡如詔。

translations.literal: Du, returning, reached Yancheng and met him; he then again entered Cai prefecture with Shouqian, measured crimes and applied punishments, not entirely according to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Du met him on the road back at Yancheng, returned with him to Cai prefecture, and punished the offenders according to the gravity of their crimes rather than carrying out the edict in full.

sentences.zh: 守謙固以詔止，度先以疏陳，乃徑赴闕下。

translations.literal: Shouqian firmly used the edict to stop him; Du first submitted a memorial explaining, then went straight to the capital below the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shouqian tried to stop him with the edict, but Du first submitted a memorial explaining his actions and then went straight to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔加度金紫光祿大夫、弘文館大學士，賜勛上柱國，封晉國公，食邑三千戶，復知政事。

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict added to Du the titles Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, bestowed the merit rank of Upper Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jin with a fief of three thousand households, and restored him to participation in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict promoted Du to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, bestowed on him the merit rank of Upper Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jin with a fief of three thousand households, and restored him to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以淮西賊平，因功臣李光顏等來朝，欲開內宴，詔六軍使修麟德殿之東廊。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong, because the Huai West rebels had been pacified and meritorious ministers such as Li Guangyan came to court, wished to hold an inner banquet and ordered the Six Armies commissioners to repair the east corridor of the Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: With the Huai West rebellion crushed and meritorious generals such as Li Guangyan coming to court, Emperor Xianzong wished to hold a palace banquet and ordered the commissioners of the Six Armies to renovate the east corridor of the Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 軍使張奉國以公費不足，出私財以助用，訴於執政。

translations.literal: The army commissioner Zhang Fengguo, because public funds were insufficient, contributed private wealth to assist the expense and complained to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The army commissioner Zhang Fengguo, finding the public funds insufficient, spent his own money to help cover the costs and appealed to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 度從容啟曰：「陛下營造，有將作監等司局，豈可使功臣破產營繕？」

translations.literal: Du calmly submitted, saying: 'Your Majesty's construction has the Directorate of Palace Buildings and other offices; how can one let meritorious ministers ruin their households to build and repair?'
translations.idiomatic: Du calmly said, "Your Majesty's building projects are the business of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and other offices. How can meritorious ministers be driven to ruin themselves paying for palace repairs?"

sentences.zh: 上怒奉國泄漏，乃令致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor, angered that Fengguo had leaked the matter, ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, furious that Zhang Fengguo had revealed the matter, ordered him to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 其浚龍首渠，起凝暉殿，雕飾綺煥，徙佛寺花木以植於庭。

translations.literal: He dredged the Longshou Canal, raised the Ninghui Hall, carved and adorned it in splendid brilliance, and moved flowers and trees from Buddhist temples to plant in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Longshou Canal, built the Ninghui Hall in lavish ornament, and transplanted flowers and trees from Buddhist temples into the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 有程異、皇甫镈者，奸纖用事，二人領度支鹽鐵，數貢羨余錢，助帝營造。

translations.literal: There were Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo, crafty and petty men wielding power; the two of them headed the Salt and Iron Commission of the Department of Public Works and repeatedly presented surplus funds to assist the emperor's construction.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo, cunning and petty men who held real power, headed the Salt and Iron Commission and repeatedly sent surplus revenue to finance the emperor's building projects.

sentences.zh: 帝又以異、镈平蔡時供饋不乏，二人並命拜同平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor also, because Yi and Bo during the pacification of Cai had supplies without shortage, ordered both appointed as co-chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also rewarded them with appointments as co-chancellors, citing their success in keeping supplies flowing during the campaign against Cai.

sentences.zh: 度延英面論曰：「程異、皇甫镈，錢穀吏耳，非代天理物之器也。

translations.literal: Du, in audience at the Yanying Hall, argued face to face, saying: 'Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo are mere grain-and-revenue clerks, not vessels for ordering all under Heaven on Heaven's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Du argued before the emperor in the Yanying Hall, "Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo are mere revenue clerks, not men fit to govern the realm on Heaven's behalf.

sentences.zh: 陛下徇耳目之欲，拔置相位，天下人騰口掉舌，以為不可，於陛下無益。

translations.literal: Your Majesty indulges the desires of ear and eye and plucks them to set in the chancellor's seat; people throughout the realm open their mouths and wag their tongues, thinking it impossible, and it is without benefit to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has elevated them to the chancellorship to gratify private whim, and people everywhere are saying it cannot stand. It does Your Majesty no good.

sentences.zh: 願徐思其宜。」

translations.literal: I wish that you would slowly consider what is fitting.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to reconsider this carefully."

sentences.zh: 帝不省納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reflect and accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 度三上疏論之，請罷己相位，上都不省。

translations.literal: Du three times submitted memorials arguing the matter and requested removal of his own chancellor's seat; the emperor completely paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Du submitted three memorials on the matter and even asked to be removed from the chancellorship, but the emperor ignored him entirely.

sentences.zh: 事見《镈傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is seen in the 'Biography of Bo.'
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded in Huangfu Bo's biography.

sentences.zh: 又賈人張陟負五坊使楊朝汶息利錢潛匿，朝汶於陟家得私簿記，有負錢人盧載初，雲是故西川節度使盧坦大夫書跡，朝汶即捕坦家人拘之。

translations.literal: Further, the merchant Zhang Zhi owed interest money to the Five Wards commissioner Yang Chaowen and hid himself secretly; Chaowen at Zhi's house obtained a private ledger, in which a debtor Lu Zaichu said it was the handwriting of the former military commissioner of West Chuan, Grandee Lu Tan; Chaowen thereupon seized Tan's family members and detained them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the merchant Zhang Zhi, who owed interest to the Five Wards commissioner Yang Chaowen, went into hiding. Chaowen found a private ledger in Zhang's house listing a debtor named Lu Zaichu, who claimed the entry was in the handwriting of the former West Chuan military commissioner Lu Tan. Chaowen immediately seized and imprisoned Tan's family.

sentences.zh: 坦男不敢申理，即以私錢償之。

translations.literal: Tan’s son did not dare plead his case and therefore paid with private money.
translations.idiomatic: Tan’s son dared not protest and paid the debt out of his own purse.

sentences.zh: 及征驗書跡，乃故鄭滑節度盧群手書也。

translations.literal: When the handwriting was examined and verified, it turned out to be the autograph of the former Zheng-Sua military commissioner Lu Qun.
translations.idiomatic: When the handwriting was examined, it proved to be the autograph of the former Zheng-Sua military commissioner Lu Qun.

sentences.zh: 坦男理其事，朝汶曰：「錢已進過，不可復得。」

translations.literal: Tan's son pleaded the matter; Chaowen said: 'The money has already been presented and passed on; it cannot be recovered.'
translations.idiomatic: When Tan's son pressed the case, Chaowen said, "The money has already been turned in to the palace treasury. It cannot be returned."

sentences.zh: 御史中丞蕭俛及諫官上疏陳其暴橫之狀，度與崔群因延英對，極言之。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Xiao Fu and remonstrating officials submitted memorials describing his violent and overbearing conduct; Du and Cui Qun, taking advantage of Yanying audience, spoke of it to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Xiao Fu and the remonstrating officials memorialized describing his brutal conduct, and Du and Cui Qun spoke out forcefully when summoned to audience in the Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 憲宗曰：「且欲與卿商量東軍，此小事我自處置。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong said: 'For now I wish to consult with you on the eastern armies; this small matter I will dispose of myself.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong said, "I wish to discuss the eastern campaign with you for now. This is a small matter that I shall handle myself."

sentences.zh: 度奏曰：「用兵，小事也；

translations.literal: Du memorialized, saying: 'Using troops is a small matter;
translations.idiomatic: Du replied, "The use of troops is a small matter;

sentences.zh: 五坊追捕平人，大事也。

translations.literal: the Five Wards pursuing and seizing ordinary people is a great matter;
translations.idiomatic: but the Five Wards hunting down ordinary citizens is a great matter;

sentences.zh: 兵事不理，只憂山東；

translations.literal: If military affairs are not managed, one need only worry about Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: If military affairs go badly, we need only worry about Shandong;

sentences.zh: 五坊使暴橫，恐亂輦轂。」

translations.literal: if the Five Wards commissioners are violent and overbearing, I fear disorder at the imperial carriage hub.'
translations.idiomatic: but if the Five Wards commissioners run rampant, I fear chaos at the very gates of the capital."

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝久方省悟，召楊朝汶數之曰：「向者為爾使我羞見宰相。」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor finally came to awareness; he summoned Yang Chaowen and reproached him, saying: 'Earlier, because of you, you made me ashamed to face the chief ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay did the emperor come to his senses. He summoned Yang Chaowen and rebuked him, saying, "Because of you I was ashamed to face my chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 遽命誅之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Chaowen executed.

sentences.zh: 初，淮、蔡既平，鎮、冀王承宗甚懼。

translations.literal: Initially, once Huai and Cai had been pacified, Wang Chengzong of Zhen and Ji was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai and Cai were pacified, Wang Chengzong of Zhen and Ji was terrified.

sentences.zh: 度遣辯士遊說，客於趙、魏間。

translations.literal: Du sent eloquent men to persuade and lobby, guests between Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Du sent skilled persuaders to work among the Zhao and Wei territories.

sentences.zh: 使說承宗，令割地入質以效順。

translations.literal: He had them persuade Chengzong to cede territory and send hostages to show submission.
translations.idiomatic: They urged Chengzong to surrender territory and send hostages as proof of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故承宗求援於田弘正，由度使客諷動之，故兵不血刃，而承宗鼠伏。

translations.literal: Therefore Chengzong sought aid from Tian Hongzheng; through Du's envoys he was prompted and stirred, and therefore without blood on the blades, Chengzong crouched like a rat.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong therefore turned to Tian Hongzheng for help, and Du's agents worked on Hongzheng until, without a blow struck, Chengzong submitted like a cowering rat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，李師道翻覆違命，詔宣武、義成、武寧、橫海四節度之師與田弘正會軍討之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Li Shidao turned treacherous and disobeyed orders; an edict ordered the armies of the four military commissioners of Xuancheng, Yicheng, Wuning, and Henghai to join Tian Hongzheng's forces and campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Li Shidao rebelled in defiance of imperial orders. An edict mobilized the armies of the Xuancheng, Yicheng, Wuning, and Henghai commissioners to join Tian Hongzheng in a campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 弘正奏請取黎陽渡河，會李光顏等軍齊進。

translations.literal: Hongzheng memorialized requesting to take Liyang to cross the river and join Li Guangyan's and other armies in advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng memorialized asking to cross the Yellow River at Liyang and advance in concert with Li Guangyan and the other armies.

sentences.zh: 帝召宰臣於延英議可否，皆曰：「閫外之事，大將制之，既有奏陳，宜遂其請。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to the Yanying Hall to discuss whether it was permissible; all said: 'Affairs beyond the frontier gate are for the great generals to decide; since there is already a memorial, his request should be granted.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to the Yanying Hall to discuss the proposal. All agreed: "Military affairs beyond the frontier are for the generals to decide. Since he has submitted a plan, his request should be granted."

sentences.zh: 度獨以為不可，奏曰：「魏博一軍，不同諸道。

translations.literal: Du alone thought it impossible and memorialized, saying: 'The Weibo army alone is not the same as the armies of the other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Du alone dissented and memorialized, "The Weibo army is not like the forces of the other circuits.

sentences.zh: 過河之後，卻退不得，便須進擊，方見成功。

translations.literal: After crossing the river, they cannot turn back and retreat; they must advance and attack before success can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Once they cross the river they cannot turn back; they must press the attack if they are to succeed.

sentences.zh: 若取黎陽渡河，既才離本界，便至滑州，徒有供餉之勞，又生顧望之勢。

translations.literal: If they take Liyang to cross the river, having just left their own territory they reach Huazhou; they would only have the labor of supplying provisions and would also create a situation of hesitation and looking back.
translations.idiomatic: If they cross at Liyang they will barely have left their own territory before reaching Huazhou, gaining nothing but supply burdens and a temptation to hesitate.

sentences.zh: 況弘正、光顏並少威斷，更相疑惑，必恐遷延。

translations.literal: Moreover Hongzheng and Guangyan both lack stern decisiveness; mutually doubting one another, delay is surely to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Hongzheng and Guangyan both lack stern decisiveness, and mutual suspicion will surely lead to delay.

sentences.zh: 然兵事不從中制一定處分。

translations.literal: Yet if military affairs do not receive a fixed disposition from central control.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the court does not issue a firm decision on military affairs from the center,

sentences.zh: 或慮不可。

translations.literal: one may fear it will not be possible.
translations.idiomatic: I fear it will not succeed.

sentences.zh: 若欲於河南持重，則不如河北養威。

translations.literal: If one wishes to hold weight in Henan south, then it is not as good as nurturing prestige north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish to hold our ground south of the river, it would be better to build our strength north of it.

sentences.zh: 不然，則且秣馬厲兵，候霜降水落，於楊劉渡河，直抵鄆州。

translations.literal: If not, then for the time being feed horses and sharpen weapons, wait until frost falls and water recedes, cross the river at Yangliu, and go straight to Yun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, let us feed the horses and sharpen the weapons, wait until the frost comes and the waters fall, cross at Yangliu, and strike straight for Yun prefecture.

sentences.zh: 但得至陽谷已來下營，則兵勢自盛，賊形自撓。」

translations.literal: If only they can encamp from Yanggu onward, then military momentum will naturally grow strong and the rebels' form will naturally bend.'
translations.idiomatic: Once our camps are established from Yanggu southward, our military momentum will grow of itself and the rebels' morale will collapse."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Your words are correct.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 乃詔弘正取楊劉渡河。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered Hongzheng to take Yangliu to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Hongzheng to cross the river at Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 及弘正軍既濟河而南，距鄆州四十里築壘，賊勢果蹙。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng's army had crossed the river and gone south, they built fortifications forty li from Yun prefecture, and the rebels' momentum indeed grew cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hongzheng's army had crossed south and built fortifications forty li from Yun prefecture, the rebel position tightened as Du had predicted.

sentences.zh: 頃之，誅師道。

translations.literal: Before long, Shidao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Shidao was executed.

sentences.zh: 度執性不回，忠於事上，時政或有所闕，靡不極言之，故為奸臣皇甫镈所構，憲宗不悅。

translations.literal: Du's disposition was steadfast and unyielding; he was loyal in serving his superior. Whenever current policy had some deficiency, there was none he did not speak of to the utmost; therefore he was framed by the treacherous minister Huangfu Bo, and Xianzong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Du was unyielding by nature and utterly loyal to the throne. Whenever he saw a flaw in current policy he spoke out without reserve, and the treacherous Huangfu Bo turned the emperor against him until Xianzong grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 十四年，檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Governor of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Garrison Commander, and Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was sent out as acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and co-chancellor, concurrently serving as governor of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the northern capital, and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，長慶元年秋，張弘靖為幽州軍所囚，田弘正於鎮州遇害，硃克融、王廷湊復亂河朔，詔度以本官充鎮州四面行營招討使。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, in the autumn of the first year of Changqing, Zhang Hongjing was imprisoned by the Youzhou army, Tian Hongzheng was killed at Zhen prefecture, Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou again threw the Hebei north into disorder, and an edict ordered Du, in his existing offices, to serve as pacification commissioner on all sides of Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong came to the throne, in the autumn of the first year of Changqing Zhang Hongjing was taken prisoner by the Youzhou army, Tian Hongzheng was murdered at Zhen prefecture, and Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou again plunged Hebei into rebellion. An edict appointed Du, retaining his existing titles, commander of the encircling pacification forces around Zhen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時驕主荒僻，輔相庸才，制置非宜，致其復亂。

translations.literal: At that time the arrogant sovereign was remote and dissolute, the assisting chancellors were mediocre talents, arrangements were inappropriate, and this caused the renewed disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had an arrogant and dissolute sovereign, mediocre chancellors, and ill-conceived policy, and so the north fell into rebellion again.

sentences.zh: 雖李光顏、烏重胤等稱為名將，以十數萬兵擊賊，無尺寸之功。

translations.literal: Although Li Guangyan, Wu Chongyin, and others were called famous generals, with several hundred thousand soldiers attacking the rebels, there was not the slightest measure of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Even famous generals such as Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin, leading armies of several hundred thousand against the rebels, won not a single meaningful victory.

sentences.zh: 蓋以勢既橫流，無能復振。

translations.literal: It was because the momentum had already flowed sideways; none could again revive it.
translations.idiomatic: The tide had already turned against the court, and nothing could restore it.

sentences.zh: 然度受命之日，搜兵補卒，不遑寢息。

translations.literal: Yet from the day Du received his commission, he gathered soldiers and replenished troops, with no leisure for sleep and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the day he received his commission Du recruited and replenished troops without pause for rest.

sentences.zh: 自董西師，臨於賊境，屠城斬將，屢以捷聞。

translations.literal: From directing the western army and pressing on the rebel border, sacking cities and beheading generals, victory reports repeatedly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He took command of the western wing, pressed the rebel border, captured cities, and killed enemy generals, and reports of victory followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 穆宗深嘉其忠款，中使撫諭無虛月，進位檢校司空，兼充押北山諸蕃使。

translations.literal: Muzong deeply praised his loyalty and sincerity; palace envoys came to comfort and instruct him not a month without exception; he was promoted to acting Grand Master of the Department of Works and concurrently appointed commissioner over the various tribes of the northern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong greatly admired his loyalty, and palace envoys came every month with imperial commendations. Du was promoted to acting Grand Master of the Department of Works and appointed commissioner over the northern frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士元稹，交結內官，求為宰相，與知樞密魏弘簡為刎頸之交。

translations.literal: At that time the Hanlin Academician Yuan Zhen, associating with inner palace officials, sought to become chancellor and was sworn-brother friends with the Commissioner of Military Affairs Wei Hongjian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Hanlin Academician Yuan Zhen cultivated ties with inner-court eunuchs in his bid for the chancellorship and was sworn brothers with Wei Hongjian, the Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 稹雖與度無憾，然頗忌前達加於己上。

translations.literal: Although Zhen had no grievance with Du, he nevertheless greatly resented senior men being placed above himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen bore Pei Du no personal grudge, yet he resented senior statesmen who outranked him.

sentences.zh: 度方用兵山東，每處置軍事，有所論奏，多為稹輩所持。

translations.literal: Du was just then using troops in Shandong; whenever he disposed of military affairs and submitted memorials, many were blocked by Zhen's faction.
translations.idiomatic: While Du was campaigning in Shandong, Yuan Zhen and his allies repeatedly blocked the memorials in which Du proposed military dispositions.

sentences.zh: 天下皆言稹恃寵熒惑上聽，度在軍上疏論之曰：臣聞主聖臣直。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm all said Zhen relied on favor to dazzle and mislead the emperor's hearing; Du, in the army, submitted a memorial arguing the matter, saying: I have heard that when the ruler is sage, the minister is straight.
translations.idiomatic: People everywhere said Yuan Zhen abused imperial favor to mislead the throne; Pei Du, still in the field, submitted a memorial of protest, saying: I have heard that when the ruler is sage, the minister is straight.

sentences.zh: 今既遇聖主，輒為直臣，上答殊私，下塞群謗，誓除國蠹，無以家為。

translations.literal: Now having met a sage ruler, I must be a straight minister — above to answer extraordinary private favor, below to stop the slander of the multitude; I swear to remove the nation's pest, and take no thought for family.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have met a sage ruler, I must be a straight minister — above to answer extraordinary private favor, below to stop the slander of the multitude; I swear to remove the nation's pest, and take no thought for family.

sentences.zh: 茍獻替之可行，何性命之足惜？

translations.literal: If beneficial remonstrance and replacement can be carried out, what is life and personhood that they are worth sparing?
translations.idiomatic: If beneficial remonstrance can be carried out, what is my life that it is worth sparing?

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下恭承丕業，光啟雄圖，方殄頑人之風，以立太平之事。
