translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, reverently receiving the great enterprise, brilliantly opening the heroic design, is just now extinguishing the ways of stubborn men to establish the affairs of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, reverently receiving the great enterprise and brilliantly opening a heroic design, is just now extinguishing the ways of stubborn men to establish the affairs of great peace.

sentences.zh: 而逆豎構亂，震驚山東；

translations.literal: Yet violent traitors have fomented rebellion, shocking Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: Yet violent traitors have fomented rebellion, shocking Shandong;

sentences.zh: 奸臣作朋，撓敗國政。

translations.literal: treacherous ministers have formed factions, thwarting and ruining state policy.
translations.idiomatic: treacherous ministers have formed factions, thwarting and ruining state policy.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲掃蕩幽、鎮，宜肅清朝廷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to sweep clean You and Zhen; you should first make the court pure and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to sweep clean You and Zhen; you should first make the court pure and clear.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 為患有大小，議事有先後。

translations.literal: As to harm, there is large and small; as to deliberation, there is before and after.
translations.idiomatic: As to harm, there is large and small; as to deliberation, there is before and after.

sentences.zh: 河朔逆賊，只亂山東；

translations.literal: The Hebei north rebels only disturb Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei north rebels only disturb Shandong;

sentences.zh: 禁闈奸臣，必亂天下。

translations.literal: treacherous ministers in the forbidden quarters are sure to disturb the realm.
translations.idiomatic: treacherous ministers in the inner palace are sure to disturb the realm.

sentences.zh: 是則河朔患小，禁闈患大。

translations.literal: Thus the Hebei north harm is small; the forbidden quarters harm is large.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Hebei north harm is small; the inner palace harm is large.

sentences.zh: 小者，臣等與諸戎臣必能翦滅；

translations.literal: The small — we ministers and the various military ministers are sure to be able to cut down and destroy;
translations.idiomatic: The lesser harm — we ministers and the various military ministers are sure to be able to cut down and destroy;

sentences.zh: 大者，非陛下制斷，非陛下覺悟，無計驅除。

translations.literal: the large — without Your Majesty's decision and without Your Majesty's awakening, there is no plan to drive them out.
translations.idiomatic: the greater — without Your Majesty's decision and without Your Majesty's awakening, there is no plan to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 今文武百僚，中外萬品，有心者無不憤忿，有口者無不咨嗟。

translations.literal: Now among the civil and military hundred officials, inside and outside the myriad ranks, those with hearts none fail to be angry and indignant; those with mouths none fail to sigh and lament.
translations.idiomatic: Now among the civil and military hundred officials, inside and outside the myriad ranks, those with hearts none fail to be angry and indignant; those with mouths none fail to sigh and lament.

sentences.zh: 直以威權方重，獎用方深，無所畏避，不敢抵觸，恐事未行禍已及，不為國計，且為身謀。

translations.literal: Only because authority and power are just now heavy and rewards and employment just now deep, they have nothing to fear or avoid and dare not oppose — fearing that before the matter is carried out calamity has already arrived, not planning for the state but scheming for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Only because authority and power are just now heavy and rewards and employment just now deep, they have nothing to fear or avoid and dare not oppose — fearing that before the matter is carried out calamity has already arrived, not planning for the state but scheming for themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣比者猶思隱忍，不願發明。

translations.literal: I, your minister, until recently still thought to endure in silence and did not wish to expose the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I, your minister, until recently still thought to endure in silence and did not wish to expose the matter.

sentences.zh: 一則以罪惡如山，怨謗如雷，伏料聖明，必自誅殛；

translations.literal: On one hand, because their crimes are like mountains and resentment and slander like thunder, I presumed on Your Majesty's sagacity that you would yourself punish and execute them;
translations.idiomatic: On one hand, because their crimes are like mountains and resentment and slander like thunder, I presumed on Your Majesty's sagacity that you would yourself punish and execute them;

sentences.zh: 一則以四方無事，萬樞且過，雖紀綱潛壞，賄賂公行，俟其貫盈，必自顛覆。

translations.literal: on the other hand, because the four quarters were untroubled and the myriad affairs could yet pass, though discipline was secretly ruined and bribery openly practiced, waiting until they brim over full they would surely overturn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: on the other hand, because the four quarters were untroubled and the myriad affairs could yet pass, though discipline was secretly ruined and bribery openly practiced, waiting until they brim over full they would surely overturn themselves.

sentences.zh: 今屬兇徒擾攘，宸衷憂軫，凡有制命，計於安危。

translations.literal: Now it falls when violent bandits are in turmoil and uproar, and the imperial heart is pained and distressed; whatever orders are issued are calculated for safety and danger.
translations.idiomatic: Now it falls when violent bandits are in turmoil and uproar, and the imperial heart is pained and distressed; whatever orders are issued are calculated for safety and danger.

sentences.zh: 痛此奸邪，恣行欺罔，幹亂聖略，非止一途。

translations.literal: I grieve that these treacherous and evil men freely practice deception and confusion, interfering with the sacred strategy — and not by one path alone.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that these treacherous and evil men freely practice deception and confusion, interfering with the sacred strategy — and not by one path alone.

sentences.zh: 又翰苑舊臣，結為朋黨，陛下聽其所說，更訪於近臣，私相計會，更唱叠和，蔽惑聰明。

translations.literal: Moreover, former Hanlin officials have banded together as a faction; Your Majesty listens to what they say and inquires further of near ministers; they privately plot together and echo and respond in layers, obscuring and bewildering clear insight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, former Hanlin officials have banded together as a faction; Your Majesty listens to what they say and inquires further of near ministers; they privately plot together and echo and respond in layers, obscuring and bewildering clear insight.

sentences.zh: 所以臣自兵興已來，所陳章疏，事皆要切，所奉書詔，多有參差。

translations.literal: Therefore since the army was raised, the memorials I have submitted have all concerned urgent matters, yet the edicts I have received have often been inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore since the army was raised, the memorials I have submitted have all concerned urgent matters, yet the edicts I have received have often been inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 惜陛下委付之意不輕，被奸臣抑損之事不少。

translations.literal: I regret that Your Majesty's trust in entrustment was not light, yet the things by which treacherous ministers suppressed and diminished me were not few.
translations.idiomatic: I regret that Your Majesty's trust in entrustment was not light, yet the things by which treacherous ministers suppressed and diminished me were not few.

sentences.zh: 臣素知佞幸，亦無讎嫌，只是昨者，臣請乘傳詣闕，面陳戎事，奸臣之徒，最所畏懼。

translations.literal: I have long known these flatterers and favorites and bear them no grudge; it is only that yesterday I requested to take the post relay to the court to state military affairs face to face — the treacherous ministers' clique feared this above all.
translations.idiomatic: I have long known these flatterers and favorites and bear them no grudge; it is only that yesterday I requested to take the post relay to the court to state military affairs face to face — the treacherous ministers' clique feared this above all.

sentences.zh: 知臣若到御坐之前，必能悉數其過，以此百計止臣此行。

translations.literal: They knew that if I came before the imperial seat I would surely be able to enumerate their faults completely; for this reason they by a hundred schemes stopped this journey of mine.
translations.idiomatic: They knew that if I came before the imperial seat I would surely be able to enumerate their faults completely; for this reason they by a hundred schemes stopped this journey of mine.

sentences.zh: 臣又請領兵齊進，逐便攻討，奸臣之黨，曲加阻礙。

translations.literal: I also requested to lead troops forward together and attack and chastise as opportunity offered; the treacherous ministers' faction twisted and added obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: I also requested to lead troops forward together and attack and chastise as opportunity offered; the treacherous ministers' faction twisted and added obstruction.

sentences.zh: 恐臣統率諸道，或有成功，進退皆受羈牽，意見悉遭蔽塞。

translations.literal: They feared that if I commanded the various circuits and achieved some success, in advance and retreat I would all be fettered and harnessed, and my views would all be blocked and sealed off.
translations.idiomatic: They feared that if I commanded the various circuits and achieved some success, in advance and retreat I would all be fettered and harnessed, and my views would all be blocked and sealed off.

sentences.zh: 復共一二憸狡，同辭合力。

translations.literal: They again joined with one or two sly and cunning men, same words and combined force.
translations.idiomatic: They again joined with one or two sly and cunning men, same words and combined force.

sentences.zh: 或兩道招撫，逗留旬時；

translations.literal: At times they would pacify and appease on two fronts, delaying for ten days;
translations.idiomatic: At times they would pacify and appease on two fronts, delaying for ten days;

sentences.zh: 或遣蔚州行營，拖曳日月。

translations.literal: at times they would dispatch the Weizhou field camp, dragging out days and months.
translations.idiomatic: at times they would dispatch the Weizhou field camp, dragging out days and months.

sentences.zh: 但欲令臣失所，使臣無成，則天下理亂，山東勝負，悉不顧矣。

translations.literal: They only wished to make me lose my place and make me achieve nothing — then the order and disorder of the realm, the victory and defeat of Shandong, they would all disregard.
translations.idiomatic: They only wished to make me lose my place and make me achieve nothing — then the order and disorder of the realm, the victory and defeat of Shandong, they would all disregard.

sentences.zh: 為臣事君，一至於此。

translations.literal: To serve one's ruler as minister — it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: To serve one's ruler as minister — it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 且陛下左右前後，忠良至多，亦有熟會典章，亦有飽諳師旅，足得任使，何獨斯人？

translations.literal: Moreover, before and behind and on Your Majesty's left and right, the loyal and good are many; some are well versed in statutes and regulations, some are fully acquainted with armies and campaigns — fully adequate for employment; why rely on this man alone?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, before and behind and on Your Majesty's left and right, the loyal and good are many; some are well versed in statutes and regulations, some are fully acquainted with armies and campaigns — fully adequate for employment; why rely on this man alone?

sentences.zh: 以臣愚見，若朝中奸臣盡去，則河朔逆賊，不討而自平；

translations.literal: In my humble view, if the treacherous ministers in court were all removed, then the Hebei north rebels would not need to be chastised and would subdue themselves;
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, if the treacherous ministers in court were all removed, then the Hebei north rebels would not need to be chastised and would subdue themselves;

sentences.zh: 若朝中奸臣尚在，則逆賊縱平無益。

translations.literal: if the treacherous ministers in court still remain, then even if the rebels were pacified it would be of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: if the treacherous ministers in court still remain, then even if the rebels were pacified it would be of no benefit.

sentences.zh: 臣讀國史，知代宗朝蕃戎侵軼，直犯都城。

translations.literal: I have read the national histories and know that in the reign of Emperor Daizong the frontier tribes raided and invaded, straight to attacking the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the national histories and know that in the reign of Emperor Daizong the frontier tribes raided and invaded, straight to attacking the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗不知，蓋被程元振蒙蔽，幾危社稷。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong did not know — it was because he was obscured by Cheng Yuanzhen — and the altars of state were nearly endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong did not know — it was because he was obscured by Cheng Yuanzhen — and the altars of state were nearly endangered.

sentences.zh: 當時柳伉，乃太常一博士耳，猶能抗表歸罪，為國除害。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Xuan was only a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, yet he was still able to submit a defiant memorial assigning guilt and remove harm for the state.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Xuan was only a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, yet he was still able to submit a defiant memorial assigning guilt and remove harm for the state.

sentences.zh: 今臣年處，兼總將相，豈肯坐觀兇邪，有曀日月。

translations.literal: Now I am in office at my years, holding both general and minister in one; how could I be willing to sit and watch violent evil obscure the sun and moon?
translations.idiomatic: Now I am in office at my years, holding both general and minister in one; how could I be willing to sit and watch violent evil obscure the sun and moon?

sentences.zh: 不勝感憤嫉惡之至！

translations.literal: I cannot bear the utmost of feeling, indignation, jealousy, and hatred!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear the utmost of feeling, indignation, jealousy, and hatred!

sentences.zh: 謹附中使趙奉國以聞。

translations.literal: I respectfully attach this through the palace envoy Zhao Fengguo to report.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully attach this through the palace envoy Zhao Fengguo to report.

sentences.zh: 倘陛下未信忠言，猶惑奸黨，伏乞出臣此表，令三事大夫與百僚集議。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty has not yet believed loyal words and still is deluded by the treacherous faction, I humbly beg that this memorial of mine be issued and that the Three Excellencies and the hundred officials assemble to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty has not yet believed loyal words and still is deluded by the treacherous faction, I humbly beg that this memorial of mine be issued and that the Three Excellencies and the hundred officials assemble to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 彼不受責，臣合伏辜，天鑒孔明，照臣肝血。

translations.literal: If they do not accept blame, I ought to accept punishment; Heaven's mirror is bright and clear — illuminate the liver and blood of your minister.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not accept blame, I ought to accept punishment; Heaven's mirror is bright and clear — illuminate the liver and blood of your minister.

sentences.zh: 但得天下之人，知臣不負陛下，則雖死之日，猶生之年。

translations.literal: If only the people of the realm know that I have not failed Your Majesty, then even on the day I die it will be as on the day I live.
translations.idiomatic: If only the people of the realm know that I have not failed Your Majesty, then even on the day I die it will be as on the day I live.

sentences.zh: 繼上三章，辭情激切。

translations.literal: He subsequently submitted three chapters in succession; the language and sentiment were impassioned and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with three more memorials, each more impassioned than the last.

sentences.zh: 穆宗雖不悅，雖懼大臣正議，乃以魏弘簡為弓箭庫使，罷元稹內職。

translations.literal: Although Muzong was displeased, although fearing the chief ministers' upright discussion, he thereupon made Wei Hongjian commissioner of the bow and arrow storehouse and removed Yuan Zhen from his inner-court duties.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was displeased, yet fearing the censure of his senior ministers he transferred Wei Hongjian to the bow and arrow storehouse and removed Yuan Zhen from his inner-court post.

sentences.zh: 然寵稹之意未衰。

translations.literal: Yet the intent to favor Zhen had not declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his favor toward Yuan Zhen did not wane.

sentences.zh: 俄拜稹平章事，尋罷度兵權，守司徒、同平章事，充東都留守。

translations.literal: Soon Zhen was appointed Grand Councilor; shortly Du's military authority was removed; he retained Situ and concurrent Grand Councilor, and was appointed Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Zhen was made Grand Councilor. Pei Du was soon stripped of military command, kept the titles of Minister of Education and concurrent Grand Councilor, and was posted as commander of the Eastern Capital garrison at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 諫官相率伏閣詣延英門者日二三。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials, leading one another, daily two or three knelt prostrate at the Yanying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Every day two or three remonstrating officials would go together to kneel in protest at the Yanying Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝知其諫，不即被召，皆上疏言：時未偃兵，度有將相全才，不宜置之散地。

translations.literal: The emperor knew they were remonstrating; he did not immediately summon them; they all submitted memorials stating: war had not yet ceased, Du possessed the full talent of a general and minister, and it was not fitting to place him in an idle post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood the protest but did not summon the officials at once. They all submitted memorials arguing that with the war not yet ended, Pei Du possessed the full gifts of both general and statesman and ought not be consigned to a post with no real authority.

sentences.zh: 帝以章疏旁午，無如之何，知人情在度，遂詔度自太原由京師赴洛。

translations.literal: The emperor, because memorials came in profusion, could do nothing about it; knowing that popular sentiment favored Du, he thereupon ordered Du to travel from Taiyuan via the capital to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Overwhelmed by the flood of memorials and unable to resist the tide of opinion favoring Du, the emperor ordered him to travel from Taiyuan by way of the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及元稹為相，請上罷兵，洗雪廷湊、克融，解深州之圍，蓋欲罷度兵柄故也。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen became chancellor he asked the emperor to cease the war, clear Wang Tingcou and Zhu Kerong, and lift the siege of Shenzhou — this was essentially in order to remove Du's military command.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Zhen became chief minister, he urged the throne to halt the campaign, absolve Wang Tingcou and Zhu Kerong, and end the siege of Shenzhou — all chiefly as a means of stripping Pei Du of military command.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，度至京師。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Du arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, Pei Du arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 既見，先敘克融、廷湊暴亂河朔，受命討賊無功；

translations.literal: Once he was received, he first recounted how Kerong and Tingcou had ravaged the Hebei north in rebellion, and that though charged to punish the rebels he had achieved no success;
translations.idiomatic: Once he was received in audience, he first recounted how Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou had ravaged the Hebei north in rebellion, and how, though charged to punish the rebels, he had achieved no success;

sentences.zh: 次陳除職東都，許令入覲。

translations.literal: Next he explained his removal to an Eastern Capital post and the permission granted him to enter court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained his transfer to an Eastern Capital post and the permission granted him to enter court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 辭和氣勁，感動左右。

translations.literal: His words were gentle in tone yet forceful in spirit, moving all who were present.
translations.idiomatic: His words were gentle in tone yet forceful in spirit, moving everyone present.

sentences.zh: 度伏奏龍墀，涕泗鳴咽，帝為之動容，口自諭之曰：「所謝知，朕於延英待卿。」

translations.literal: Du prostrated himself on the imperial steps, weeping and choking with sobs; the emperor was moved and personally spoke to reassure him, saying: "Your thanks are understood. I shall receive you at the Yanying Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du prostrated himself on the imperial steps, weeping and choking with sobs. The emperor was moved and spoke to reassure him in person: "Your thanks are understood. I shall receive you at the Yanying Hall."

sentences.zh: 初，人以度無左右之助，為奸邪排擯，雖度勛德，恐不能感動人主。

translations.literal: At first people thought Du had no supporters at court and had been excluded by treacherous factions; though his merit and virtue were great, they feared he could not move the sovereign's heart.
translations.idiomatic: At first people believed Pei Du had no allies at court and had been pushed aside by treacherous factions. Though his merit and virtue were great, they feared he could not move the sovereign's heart.

sentences.zh: 及度奏河北事，慷慨激切，揚於殿廷，在位者無不聳動。

translations.literal: When Du presented the Hebei affair, he spoke with passionate urgency, his voice ringing through the hall; none of those in attendance failed to be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: When Du presented the Hebei affair, he spoke with passionate urgency, his voice ringing through the hall. None of those in attendance failed to be stirred.

sentences.zh: 雖武夫貴介，亦有咨嗟出涕者。

translations.literal: Even military men of noble birth were moved to sigh and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Even military men of noble birth were moved to sigh and shed tears.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以度守司徒、揚州大都督府長史，充淮南節度使，進階光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next day Du was ordered to retain Situ, serve as chief administrator of Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture, and take office as military commissioner of Huainan, with promotion to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Du was ordered to retain the title of Minister of Education, serve as chief administrator of Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture, and take office as military commissioner of Huainan, with promotion to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時朱克融、王廷湊雖受朝廷節鉞，未解深州之圍。

translations.literal: At the time, although Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou had received court commissions, they had not lifted the siege of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, although Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou had received court commissions, they had not lifted the siege of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 度初發太原，與二鎮書，諭以大義。

translations.literal: When Du first set out from Taiyuan he wrote to the two garrisons, instructing them in the larger principles at stake.
translations.idiomatic: When Du first set out from Taiyuan, he wrote to the two garrisons, instructing them in the larger principles at stake.

sentences.zh: 克融解圍而去，廷湊亦退舍。

translations.literal: Kerong lifted the siege and withdrew; Tingcou also pulled back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong lifted the siege and withdrew; Wang Tingcou also pulled back.

sentences.zh: 有中使自深州來言之，穆宗甚喜。

translations.literal: An inner-court envoy came from Shenzhou with the news; Muzong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: An inner-court envoy came from Shenzhou with the news; Emperor Muzong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 即日又遣中使往深州取牛元翼，更命度致書與廷湊。

translations.literal: That same day he again dispatched an envoy to Shenzhou to fetch Niu Yuanyi, and further ordered Du to send another letter to Tingcou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he again dispatched an envoy to Shenzhou to fetch Niu Yuanyi, and further ordered Du to send another letter to Wang Tingcou.

sentences.zh: 度沿路奉詔，中使得度書云：「朝謝後，即歸留務。

translations.literal: As Du traveled along the route carrying out his orders, the envoy obtained from Du a letter saying: "After paying court thanks I shall at once return to my garrison duties.
translations.idiomatic: As Du traveled along the route carrying out his orders, the envoy obtained from him a letter saying: "After paying court thanks I shall at once return to my garrison duties.

sentences.zh: 恐廷湊知度無兵權，即背前約，請度易之。」

translations.literal: Fearing that if Tingcou learned Du had no military authority he would break his earlier pledge, he asked Du to revise the letter."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that if Wang Tingcou learned Du no longer held military authority he would break his earlier pledge, the envoy asked Du to revise the letter."

sentences.zh: 中使乃進度書草，具奏其事。

translations.literal: The envoy then submitted the draft of Du's letter and fully reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy then submitted the draft of Du's letter and fully reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及度至京師，進退明辯，帝方憂深州之圍，遂授度淮南節度使。

translations.literal: When Du reached the capital his reasoning on what to advance and what to withdraw was clear; the emperor, still worried about the siege of Shenzhou, thereupon appointed Du military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Du reached the capital, his reasoning on what to advance and what to withdraw was clear. The emperor, still worried about the siege of Shenzhou, thereupon appointed him military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 先是，監軍使劉承偕恃寵淩節度使劉悟，三軍憤發大噪，擒承偕，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Previously, the army supervisor Liu Chengjie, relying on imperial favor, looked down on the military commissioner Liu Wu; the three armies, inflamed with anger, raised a great clamor, seized Chengjie, and meant to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the army supervisor Liu Chengjie, relying on imperial favor, looked down on the military commissioner Liu Wu. The three armies, inflamed with anger, raised a great clamor, seized Chengjie, and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 已殺其二傔，悟救之獲免，而囚承偕。

translations.literal: They had already killed two of his attendants; Wu rescued him and he escaped death, but Chengjie was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: They had already killed two of his attendants. Liu Wu rescued him and he escaped death, but Chengjie was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 詔遣歸京，悟托以軍情，不時奉詔。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chengjie sent back to the capital, but Wu pleaded military circumstances and did not comply in good time.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chengjie sent back to the capital, but Liu Wu pleaded military circumstances and did not comply in good time.

sentences.zh: 至是，宰臣延英奏事，度亦在列。

translations.literal: At this point the chief ministers were reporting affairs at the Yanying Hall, and Du was among them.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the chief ministers were reporting affairs at the Yanying Hall, and Du was among them.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂度曰：「劉悟拘承偕而不遣，如何處置？」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Du and said: "Liu Wu is holding Chengjie and will not release him. How should this be handled?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Du and said: "Liu Wu is holding Chengjie and will not release him. How should this be handled?"

sentences.zh: 度辭以蕃臣不合議軍國事。

translations.literal: Du declined on the ground that as a frontier appointee he ought not debate state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Du declined on the ground that as a frontier appointee he ought not debate state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上固問之，且曰：「劉悟負我，我以僕射寵之，近又賜絹五百萬疋，不思報功，翻縱軍眾淩辱監軍，我實難奈此事。」

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him further and said: "Liu Wu has betrayed me. I showered him with the title of Vice Director of the Left and recently granted five million bolts of silk, yet instead of repaying me with loyal service he let his troops humiliate the army supervisor. I truly find this situation hard to bear."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him further and said: "Liu Wu has betrayed me. I showered him with the title of Vice Director of the Left and recently granted five million bolts of silk, yet instead of repaying me with loyal service he let his troops humiliate the army supervisor. I truly find this situation hard to bear."

sentences.zh: 度對曰：「承偕在昭義不法，臣盡知之，昨劉悟在行營與臣書，數論其事。

translations.literal: Du replied: "Chengjie's misconduct in Zhaoyi is fully known to me. Not long ago Liu Wu wrote to me from the field camp, repeatedly discussing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Du replied: "Chengjie's misconduct in Zhaoyi is fully known to me. Not long ago Liu Wu wrote to me from the field camp, repeatedly discussing the matter.

sentences.zh: 是時有中使趙弘亮在臣軍，仍持悟書將去，欲自奏，不知奏否？」

translations.literal: At that time the envoy Zhao Hongliang was with my army, carrying Wu's letter away, intending to report it himself — I do not know whether he reported it or not?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the envoy Zhao Hongliang was with my army, carrying Liu Wu's letter away and intending to report it himself. I do not know whether he reported it or not."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我都不知，悟何不密奏其事，我豈不能處置？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I knew nothing of this. Why did Wu not report it secretly? Could I not have handled it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I knew nothing of this. Why did Liu Wu not report it secretly? Could I not have handled it?"

sentences.zh: 度曰：「劉悟武臣，不知大臣體例。

translations.literal: Du said: "Liu Wu is a military officer and does not know the protocols expected of high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "Liu Wu is a military officer and does not know the protocols expected of high ministers.

sentences.zh: 雖然，臣竊以悟縱有密奏，陛下必不能處置。

translations.literal: Even so, I privately believe that even had Wu made a secret report, Your Majesty would certainly not have been able to act on it.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, I privately believe that even had Liu Wu made a secret report, Your Majesty would certainly not have been able to act on it.

sentences.zh: 今日事狀如此，臣等面論，陛下猶未能決，悟單辭豈能動聖聽哉？」

translations.literal: Today's situation is as you see. Even with us debating face to face Your Majesty still cannot decide — how could Wu's word alone have moved the imperial ear?"
translations.idiomatic: Today's situation is as you see. Even with us debating face to face Your Majesty still cannot decide — how could Liu Wu's word alone have moved the imperial ear?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「前事勿論，直言此時如何處置？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do not discuss the past. Tell me plainly how it should be handled now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do not discuss the past. Tell me plainly how it should be handled now."

sentences.zh: 度曰：「陛下必欲收忠義之心，使天下戎臣為陛下死節，唯有下半紙詔書，言任使不明，致承偕亂法如此，令悟集三軍斬之。

translations.literal: Du said: "If Your Majesty truly wishes to win the hearts of the loyal and righteous and make military men throughout the realm die for you in faithful service, there is only one course: issue half a sheet of edict saying that your appointment was ill-chosen, that this caused Chengjie to break the law so flagrantly, and order Liu Wu to assemble the three armies and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "If Your Majesty truly wishes to win the hearts of the loyal and righteous and make military men throughout the realm die for you in faithful service, there is only one course: issue half a sheet of edict saying that your appointment was ill-chosen, that this caused Chengjie to break the law so flagrantly, and order Liu Wu to assemble the three armies and execute him.

sentences.zh: 如此，則萬方畢命，群盜破膽，天下無事矣。

translations.literal: If you do this, all the realm will pour out their lives for you, every rebel will lose heart, and the empire will be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: If you do this, all the realm will pour out their lives for you, every rebel will lose heart, and the empire will be at peace.

sentences.zh: 茍不能如此，雖與劉悟改官賜絹，臣亦恐於事無益。」

translations.literal: If you cannot do this, then even if you change Liu Wu's titles and grant him more silk, I fear it will do no good.'
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot do this, then even if you change Liu Wu's titles and grant him more silk, I fear it will do no good."

sentences.zh: 上俛首良久，曰：「朕不惜承偕。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed his head for a long while and said, "I would not begrudge Chengjie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed his head for a long while and said, "I would not begrudge Chengjie.

sentences.zh: 緣是太后養子，今被囚縶，太后未知，如卿處置未得，可更議其宜。」

translations.literal: But he is the Empress Dowager's adopted son. He is now imprisoned and the Empress Dowager does not know. If your proposed handling will not do, we may discuss a more suitable course."
translations.idiomatic: But he is the Empress Dowager's adopted son. He is now imprisoned and the Empress Dowager does not know. If your proposed handling will not do, we may discuss a more suitable course."

sentences.zh: 度與王播等復奏曰：「但配流遠惡處，承偕必得出。」

translations.literal: Du and Wang Bo and the others again reported: "If he is simply exiled to some remote and harsh place, Chengjie will surely be released."
translations.idiomatic: Du and Wang Bo and the others again reported: "If he is simply exiled to some remote and harsh place, Chengjie will surely be released."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，承偕果得歸。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, and Chengjie was indeed able to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Chengjie was indeed able to return.

sentences.zh: 度方受冊司徒，徐州奏節度副使王智興自河北行營率師還，逐節度使崔群，自稱留後。

translations.literal: Just as Du was receiving investiture as Situ, Xuzhou reported that the deputy military commissioner Wang Zhixing, returning from the Hebei field camp at the head of his troops, had driven out the military commissioner Cui Qun and declared himself interim commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Du was receiving investiture as Minister of Education, Xuzhou reported that the deputy military commissioner Wang Zhixing, returning from the Hebei field camp at the head of his troops, had driven out the military commissioner Cui Qun and declared himself interim commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷駭懼，即日宣制，以度守司徒、同平章事，復知政事。

translations.literal: The court was shocked and alarmed; that same day an edict was promulgated appointing Du to retain Situ and concurrent Grand Councilor, restoring him to governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court was shocked and alarmed. That same day an edict was promulgated appointing Du to retain the title of Minister of Education and concurrent Grand Councilor, restoring him to governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 乃以宰相王播代度鎮淮南。

translations.literal: Wang Bo was then appointed in Du's place to command Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Bo was then appointed in Du's place to command Huainan.

sentences.zh: 度與李逢吉素不協。

translations.literal: Du and Li Fengji had never been on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du and Li Fengji had never been on good terms.

sentences.zh: 度自太原入朝，而惡度者以逢吉善於陰計，足能構度，乃自襄陽召逢吉入朝，為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Du entered court from Taiyuan, those who hated Du, believing Fengji skilled in covert schemes and fully capable of framing Du, summoned Fengji from Xiangyang to court as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Du entered court from Taiyuan, those who hated him, believing Li Fengji skilled in covert schemes and fully capable of framing Du, summoned Fengji from Xiangyang to court as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 度既復知政事，而魏弘簡、劉承偕之黨在禁中。

translations.literal: Once Du had again taken up governing affairs, the factions of Wei Hongjian and Liu Chengjie remained within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once Du had again taken up governing affairs, the factions of Wei Hongjian and Liu Chengjie remained within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 逢吉用族子仲言之謀，因醫人鄭註與中尉王守澄交結，內官皆為之助。

translations.literal: Fengji employed the scheme of his clansman Zhongyan: through the physician Zheng Zhu he cultivated ties with the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng, and the inner officials all lent their support.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji employed the scheme of his clansman Li Zhongyan: through the physician Zheng Zhu he cultivated ties with the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng, and the inner officials all lent their support.

sentences.zh: 五月，左神策軍奏告事人李賞稱和王府司馬於方受元稹所使，結客欲刺裴度。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Left Divine Strategy Army reported that the informant Li Shang claimed the Prince of He's chief secretary Yu Fang, at Yuan Zhen's instigation, had recruited guests intending to assassinate Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Left Divine Strategy Army reported that the informant Li Shang claimed the Prince of He's chief secretary Yu Fang, at Yuan Zhen's instigation, had recruited guests intending to assassinate Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 詔左僕射韓臯、給事中鄭覃與李逢吉三人鞫於方之獄。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Vice Director of the Left Han Gao, the Supervising Secretary Zheng Tan, and Li Fengji — three men — to investigate Yu Fang's case.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Vice Director of the Left Han Gao, the Supervising Secretary Zheng Tan, and Li Fengji — three men — to investigate Yu Fang's case.

sentences.zh: 未竟，罷元稹為同州刺史，罷度為左僕射，李逢吉代度為宰相。

translations.literal: Before the case was finished, Yuan Zhen was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou, Du was demoted to Vice Director of the Left, and Li Fengji replaced Du as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before the case was finished, Yuan Zhen was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou, Pei Du was demoted to Vice Director of the Left, and Li Fengji replaced Du as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 自是，逢吉之黨李仲言、張又新、李續等，內結中官，外扇朝士，立朋黨以沮度，時號「八關十六子」，皆交結相關之人數也。

translations.literal: From this point the Fengji clique — Li Zhongyan, Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, and others — colluded with inner officials, inflamed court officials without, and formed a faction to obstruct Du. They were at the time called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons" — all men bound together in mutual connivance.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Li Fengji's clique — Li Zhongyan, Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, and others — colluded with inner officials, inflamed court officials without, and formed a faction to obstruct Du. They were at the time called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons" — all men bound together in mutual connivance.

sentences.zh: 而度之醜譽日聞，俄出度為山南西道節度使，不帶平章事。

translations.literal: And reports of scandal concerning Du spread daily; before long Du was sent out as military commissioner of the Mountain South West Circuit, without the Grand Councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of scandal concerning Du spread daily, and before long he was sent out as military commissioner of the Mountain South West Circuit, without the Grand Councilor title.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年，襄陽節度使牛元翼卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing, the Xiangyang military commissioner Niu Yuanyi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changqing, the Xiangyang military commissioner Niu Yuanyi died.

sentences.zh: 其家先在鎮州，朝廷累遣中使取之，王廷湊遷延不遣。

translations.literal: His family had remained in Zhenzhou; the court repeatedly sent envoys to fetch them, but Wang Tingcou delayed and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: His family had remained in Zhenzhou. The court repeatedly sent envoys to fetch them, but Wang Tingcou delayed and would not release them.

sentences.zh: 至是，聞元翼卒，乃盡屠其家。

translations.literal: When he learned Yuanyi had died, he slaughtered the entire family.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Yuanyi had died, he slaughtered the entire family.

sentences.zh: 昭湣皇帝聞之，嗟惋累日，因嘆宰輔非才，致奸臣悖逆如此。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong heard of it, he sighed in grief for days, lamenting that his chief ministers lacked talent and had allowed treacherous subjects to rebel so brazenly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong heard of it, he sighed in grief for days, lamenting that his chief ministers lacked talent and had allowed treacherous subjects to rebel so brazenly.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士韋處厚上言曰：臣聞汲黯在朝，淮南不敢謀叛；

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou submitted a memorial, saying: I have heard that when Ji An was at court, Huainan did not dare to plot rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou submitted a memorial, saying: I have heard that when Ji An was at court, Huainan did not dare to plot rebellion;

sentences.zh: 幹木處魏，諸侯不敢加兵。

translations.literal: when Gan Mu was in Wei, the feudal lords did not dare to raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: when Gan Mu was in Wei, the feudal lords did not dare to raise arms.

sentences.zh: 王霸之理，皆以一士而止百萬之師，以一賢而制千里之難。

translations.literal: The principle of true kingship and hegemony is that all use one scholar to stop an army of a million and one worthy man to control difficulty for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of true kingship is that one worthy man can stop an army of a million and master difficulty across a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以裴度勛高中夏，聲播外夷，廷湊、克融皆憚其用，吐蕃、回鶻悉服其名。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Pei Du's merit is high in central China and his fame spreads to outer barbarians; Wang Tingcou and Zhu Kerong both fear his employment, and Tibet and the Uyghurs all submit to his name.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Pei Du's merit is high in central China and his fame spreads to outer barbarians; Wang Tingcou and Zhu Kerong both fear his employment, and Tibet and the Uyghurs all submit to his name.

sentences.zh: 今若置之巖廊，委其參決，西夷北虜，未測中華；

translations.literal: Now if he were placed in the lofty hall and entrusted with deliberation and decision, the western barbarians and northern enemies would not be able to measure China;
translations.idiomatic: Now if he were placed in the lofty hall of government and entrusted with deliberation and decision, the western barbarians and northern enemies would not be able to measure China;

sentences.zh: 河北山東，必稟廟算。

translations.literal: Hebei and Shandong would surely defer to the court's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei and Shandong would surely defer to the court's plans.

sentences.zh: 況幽、鎮未靜，尤資重臣。

translations.literal: Moreover, You and Zhen are not yet pacified — all the more must we rely on a weighty minister.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, You and Zhen are not yet pacified — all the more must we rely on a weighty minister.

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：「人離而聽之則愚，合而聽之則聖。」

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said, 'When men are apart and one listens, one is foolish; when one listens together, one is sage.'
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said, 'When men are apart and one listens, one is foolish; when one listens together, one is sage.'

sentences.zh: 理亂之本，非有他術，順人則理，違人則亂。

translations.literal: The root of order and disorder has no other art: accord with the people and there is order; go against the people and there is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The root of order and disorder has no other art: accord with the people and there is order; go against the people and there is disorder.

sentences.zh: 伏承陛下當食嘆息，恨無蕭、曹。

translations.literal: I humbly receive that Your Majesty at meals sighs, regretting that there are no Xiao He or Cao Shen.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly receive that Your Majesty at meals sighs, regretting that there are no Xiao He or Cao Shen.

sentences.zh: 今有一裴度尚不留驅使，此馮生所以感悟漢文，雲雖有廉頗、李牧不能用也。

translations.literal: Now there is one Pei Du whom you still do not keep for employment — this is why Feng Tang was moved regarding Emperor Wen of Han, saying that though there were Lian Po and Li Mu, they could not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Now there is one Pei Du whom you still do not keep for employment — this is why Feng Tang was moved regarding Emperor Wen of Han, saying that though there were Lian Po and Li Mu, they could not be employed.

sentences.zh: 夫禦宰相，當委之信之，親之禮之。

translations.literal: As for governing with a chief minister, you should entrust him, trust him, draw him close, and honor him with rites.
translations.idiomatic: As for governing with a chief minister, you should entrust him, trust him, draw him close, and honor him with rites.

sentences.zh: 如於事不效，於國無勞，則置之散僚，黜之遠郡。

translations.literal: If in affairs there is no effect and for the state there is no labor, then place him among idle officials and dismiss him to a distant commandery.
translations.idiomatic: If in affairs there is no effect and for the state there is no labor, then place him among idle officials and dismiss him to a distant commandery.

sentences.zh: 如此，則在位者不敢不勵，將進者不敢茍求。

translations.literal: In this way, those in office would not dare fail to exert themselves, and those about to advance would not dare seek advancement carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, those in office would not dare fail to exert themselves, and those about to advance would not dare seek advancement carelessly.

sentences.zh: 陛下存終始之分，但不永棄，則君臣之厚也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty preserves the distinction of beginning and end, only not abandoning forever — that is the thickness of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty preserves the distinction of beginning and end, only not abandoning forever — that is the depth of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 今進皆負四海責望，退不失六部尚書，不肖者無因而勸。

translations.literal: Now in advancing they all bear the expectations and hopes of the four seas; in retreating they lose no more than Minister of one of the Six Ministries — the unworthy have no opening thereby to be encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Now in advancing they all bear the expectations and hopes of the four seas; in retreating they lose no more than Minister of one of the Six Ministries — the unworthy have no opening thereby to be encouraged.

sentences.zh: 臣與李逢吉素無讎嫌，臣嘗被裴度因事貶黜。

translations.literal: I and Li Fengji have long had no grudge; I was once demoted and dismissed by Pei Du on account of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji and I have long had no grudge; I was once demoted and dismissed by Pei Du on account of an affair.

sentences.zh: 今之所陳，上答聖明，下達君議，披肝感激，伏地涕流。

translations.literal: What I now state is above to answer sagacious clarity, below to reach the deliberation of the gentlemen — laying bare my liver in gratitude, prostrate on the ground with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: What I now state is above to answer sagacious clarity, below to reach the deliberation of the gentlemen — laying bare my liver in gratitude, prostrate on the ground with streaming tears.

sentences.zh: 伏望鑒臣愛君，矜臣體國，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will discern my love of the ruler and pity my devotion to the state — then the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope you will discern my love of the ruler and pity my devotion to the state — then the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 昭湣愕然省悟，見度奏狀不帶平章事，謂處厚曰：「度曾為宰相，何無平章事？」

translations.literal: Muzong started in sudden realization. Seeing that Du's memorial bore no Grand Councilor title, he said to Chuhou: "Du was once a chancellor — why does he lack the Grand Councilor title?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong started in sudden realization. Seeing that Du's memorial bore no Grand Councilor title, he said to Wei Chuhou: "Pei Du was once a chancellor — why does he lack the Grand Councilor title?"

sentences.zh: 處厚因奏：「為逢吉所擠，度自僕射出鎮興元，遂於舊使銜中減落。」

translations.literal: Chuhou then reported: "Ousted by Fengji, when Du left the capital as Vice Director to take command at Xingyuan, the old commission title was simply struck off."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou then reported: "Ousted by Li Fengji, when Du left the capital as Vice Director to take command at Xingyuan, the old commission title was simply struck off."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何至是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could it go so far?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How could it go so far?"

sentences.zh: 翌日下制，復兼同平章事。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was issued restoring the concurrent Grand Councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict was issued restoring the concurrent Grand Councilor title.

sentences.zh: 然逢吉之黨，巧為毀沮，恐度復用。

translations.literal: Yet Fengji's clique craftily spread slander and obstructed him, fearing Du might be recalled to office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Fengji's clique craftily spread slander and obstructed him, fearing Du might be recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 有陳留人武昭者，性果敢而辯舌。

translations.literal: There was one Wu Zhao of Chenliu — bold and quick-tongued by nature.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Wu Zhao of Chenliu — bold and quick-tongued by nature.

sentences.zh: 度之討淮西也，昭求進於軍門，乃令入蔡州說吳元濟。

translations.literal: When Du campaigned against Huai-West, Zhao sought advancement at the army gate; Du had him enter Caizhou to persuade Wu Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: When Du campaigned against Huai-West, Zhao sought advancement at the army gate. Du had him enter Caizhou to persuade Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 元濟臨之以兵，昭氣色自若，善待而還。

translations.literal: Yuanji confronted him with troops, but Zhao's composure never faltered; Yuanji treated him well and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji confronted him with troops, but Zhao's composure never faltered. Yuanji treated him well and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 度以為可用，署之軍職，隨度鎮太原，奏授石州刺史。

translations.literal: Du deemed him usable, appointed him to an army post, and when Du took command at Taiyuan recommended him for appointment as prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du deemed him usable and appointed him to an army post. When Du took command at Taiyuan, he recommended Zhao for appointment as prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 罷郡，除袁王府長史。

translations.literal: When his prefectural term ended, he was made chief secretary of the Prince of Yuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: When his prefectural term ended, he was made chief secretary of the Prince of Yuan's household.

sentences.zh: 昭既在散位，心微悒郁，而有怨逢吉之言。

translations.literal: Now that Zhao held an idle post, he was somewhat morose, and he spoke words of resentment against Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhao held an idle post, he was somewhat morose, and he spoke words of resentment against Li Fengji.

sentences.zh: 而奸邪之黨，使衛尉卿劉遵古從人安再榮告事，言武昭欲謀害李逢吉。

translations.literal: The treacherous faction had the Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Liu Zungu send his follower An Zairong as informant, claiming Wu Zhao intended to plot against Li Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: The treacherous faction had the Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Liu Zungu send his follower An Zairong as informant, claiming Wu Zhao intended to plot against Li Fengji.

sentences.zh: 獄具，而武昭死，蓋欲訐度舊事以汙之也。

translations.literal: When the case was complete Wu Zhao died in custody — evidently an attempt to drag up old matters concerning Du and smear him.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete Wu Zhao died in custody — evidently an attempt to drag up old matters concerning Du and smear him.

sentences.zh: 然士君子公論，皆佑度而罪逢吉。

translations.literal: Yet among cultivated gentlemen the public consensus sided with Du and condemned Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among cultivated gentlemen the public consensus sided with Du and condemned Li Fengji.

sentences.zh: 天子漸明其端，每中使過興元，必傳密旨撫諭，且有征還之約。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven gradually perceived the truth; whenever an envoy passed through Xingyuan he always carried secret instructions of consolation, and there was even a pledge to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually perceived the truth. Whenever an envoy passed through Xingyuan he always carried secret instructions of consolation, and there was even a pledge to recall him.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年十一月，度疏請入覲京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli, Du submitted a memorial requesting permission to enter the capital for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Baoli, Du submitted a memorial requesting permission to enter the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，度至，帝禮遇隆厚，數日，宣制復知政事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Du arrived; the emperor received him with great honor, and within days an edict restored him to governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Du arrived. The emperor received him with great honor, and within days an edict restored him to governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 而逢吉黨有左拾遺張權輿者，尤出死力。

translations.literal: Among Fengji's faction one Left Reminder named Zhang Quanyu exerted himself to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Among Li Fengji's faction one Left Reminder named Zhang Quanyu exerted himself to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 度自興元請入朝也，權輿上疏曰：「度名應圖讖，宅據岡原，不召自來，其心可見。」

translations.literal: When Du requested to enter court from Xingyuan, Quanyu submitted a memorial: "Du's name matches prophetic texts, his residence occupies a hill ridge, and he came without being summoned — his intentions are plain to see."
translations.idiomatic: When Du requested to enter court from Xingyuan, Zhang Quanyu submitted a memorial: "Pei Du's name matches prophetic texts, his residence occupies a hill ridge, and he came without being summoned — his intentions are plain to see."

sentences.zh: 先是奸黨忌度，作謠辭云：「非衣小兒坦其腹，天上有口被驅逐。」

translations.literal: Earlier the treacherous faction, resentful of Du, had composed a rhyme: "The child in broadcloth bares his belly; the mouth in heaven is driven away."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the treacherous faction, resentful of Du, had composed a rhyme: "The child in broadcloth bares his belly; the mouth in heaven is driven away."

sentences.zh: 「天口」言度嘗平吳元濟也。

translations.literal: "Mouth in heaven" refers to Du's past pacification of Wu Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: "Mouth in heaven" refers to Du's past pacification of Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 又帝城東西，橫亙六崗，合《易象乾》卦之數。

translations.literal: Moreover east and west of the imperial city six ridges ran crosswise, matching the number of lines in the Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover east and west of the imperial city six ridges ran crosswise, matching the number of lines in the Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 度平樂裏第，偶當第五崗，故權輿取為語辭。

translations.literal: Du's Pingyue Lane residence happened to occupy the fifth ridge, which Quanyu seized upon for his accusatory language.
translations.idiomatic: Du's Pingyue Lane residence happened to occupy the fifth ridge, which Zhang Quanyu seized upon for his accusatory language.

sentences.zh: 昭湣雖少年，深明其誣謗，獎度之意不衰，奸邪無能措言。

translations.literal: Though Muzong was still young, he understood the slander clearly; his intent to reward Du did not fade, and the treacherous faction could find no opening.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Muzong was still young, he understood the slander clearly. His intent to reward Du did not fade, and the treacherous faction could find no opening.

sentences.zh: 時昭湣欲行幸洛陽，宰相李逢吉及兩省諫官，累疏論列，帝正色曰：「朕去意已定。

translations.literal: At this time Muzong wished to make a progress to Luoyang; Chancellor Li Fengji and remonstrating officials of the two departments repeatedly submitted memorials in protest, but the emperor said sternly: "My decision to go is already made.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Muzong wished to make a progress to Luoyang. Chancellor Li Fengji and remonstrating officials of the two departments repeatedly submitted memorials in protest, but the emperor said sternly: "My decision to go is already made.

sentences.zh: 其從官宮人，悉令自備糗糧，不勞百姓供饋。」

translations.literal: My attendant officials and palace women shall all provide their own provisions; the people need not supply us."
translations.idiomatic: My attendant officials and palace women shall all provide their own provisions; the people need not supply us."

sentences.zh: 逢吉頓首言曰：「東都千里而近，宮闕具存，以時巡遊，固亦常典。

translations.literal: Fengji said, bowing his head: "The Eastern Capital is only a thousand li away, the palaces stand intact, and a seasonal progress is indeed established custom.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji said, bowing his head: "The Eastern Capital is only a thousand li away, the palaces stand intact, and a seasonal progress is indeed established custom.

sentences.zh: 但以法駕一動，事須備儀，千乘萬騎，不可減省。

translations.literal: But once the imperial carriage moves, the full protocol must be observed; a host of a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen cannot be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: But once the imperial carriage moves, the full protocol must be observed. A host of a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen cannot be reduced.

sentences.zh: 縱不費用絕廣，亦須豐儉得宜，豈可自備糗糧，頓失大體？

translations.literal: Even if the expense is not utterly vast, outlay must be balanced between lavishness and restraint — how could officials bring their own rations without gravely compromising imperial dignity?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the expense is not utterly vast, outlay must be balanced between lavishness and restraint. How could officials bring their own rations without gravely compromising imperial dignity?

sentences.zh: 今干戈未甚戢，邊鄙未甚寧，恐人心動搖，伏乞稍回宸慮。」

translations.literal: War has not fully ceased and the frontier is not fully secure; I fear hearts may waver — I humbly beg Your Majesty to reconsider."
translations.idiomatic: War has not fully ceased and the frontier is not fully secure. I fear hearts may waver — I humbly beg Your Majesty to reconsider."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，令度支員外郎盧貞往東都已來，檢計行宮及洛陽大內。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen and ordered the Bureau of Revenue's vice-director Lu Zhen to go east and inspect the travel palaces and Luoyang's inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and ordered the Bureau of Revenue's vice-director Lu Zhen to go east and inspect the travel palaces and Luoyang's inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方懷憂恐，會度自興元來，因延英奏事，帝語及巡幸。

translations.literal: The court was still anxious and alarmed when Du arrived from Xingyuan; during business at the Yanying Hall the emperor spoke of the planned progress.
translations.idiomatic: The court was still anxious and alarmed when Du arrived from Xingyuan. During business at the Yanying Hall the emperor spoke of the planned progress.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「國家營創兩都，蓋備巡幸。

translations.literal: Du said: "The empire established two capitals precisely to accommodate such progresses.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "The empire established two capitals precisely to accommodate such progresses.

sentences.zh: 然自艱難已來，此事遂絕。

translations.literal: But since the years of turmoil this practice has ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: But since the years of turmoil this practice has ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 東都宮闕及六軍營壘、百司廨署，悉多荒廢。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital's palaces, the Six Armies' camps, and the offices of the hundred bureaus are largely in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital's palaces, the Six Armies' camps, and the offices of the hundred bureaus are largely in ruin.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲行幸，亦須稍稍修葺。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must make the journey, repairs must first be carried out gradually.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must make the journey, repairs must first be carried out gradually.

sentences.zh: 一年半歲後，方可議行。」

translations.literal: Only after a year or a season should the trip be considered."
translations.idiomatic: Only after a year or a season should the trip be considered."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「群臣意不及此，但雲不合去。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My ministers' thinking has not reached this far — they only say I ought not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "My ministers' thinking has not reached this far — they only say I ought not go.

sentences.zh: 若如卿奏，不行亦得止後期。」

translations.literal: If as you memorialized, even if I do not go, I can still cancel the later progress."
translations.idiomatic: If we follow your memorial, even if I do not make the journey, I can still cancel the later progress."

sentences.zh: 旋又硃克融、史憲誠各請以丁匠五千，助修東都，帝遂停東幸。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Zhu Kerong and Shi Xiancheng each requested five thousand corvée laborers to help repair the Eastern Capital, and the emperor then halted the eastern progress.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Zhu Kerong and Shi Xiancheng each requested five thousand corvée laborers to help repair the Eastern Capital, and the emperor then halted the eastern progress.

sentences.zh: 幽州硃克融執留賜春衣使楊文端，奏稱衣段疏薄；

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou detained and held the Spring Clothing envoy Yang Wenduan, memorializing that the cloth sections were thin and shoddy;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou detained the Spring Clothing envoy Yang Wenduan and memorialized that the cloth sections granted were thin and shoddy;

sentences.zh: 又奏今歲三軍春衣不足，擬於度支請給一季春衣，約三十萬端匹；

translations.literal: He also memorialized that this year's spring clothing for the three armies was insufficient, planning to request from the Bureau of Revenue provision of one season's spring clothing, about three hundred thousand rolls of cloth;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that this year's spring clothing for the three armies was insufficient and proposed requesting from the Bureau of Revenue one season's supply of spring clothing, roughly three hundred thousand rolls of cloth;

sentences.zh: 又請助丁匠五千修東都。

translations.literal: He also requested five thousand corvée laborers to help repair the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested five thousand corvée laborers to help repair the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 上憂其不遜，問宰臣曰：「克融所奏，如何處分？

translations.literal: The emperor, worried by his insubordination, asked the chief ministers: "How should Kerong's memorial be handled?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, alarmed by his insubordination, asked the chief ministers: "How should Kerong's memorial be handled?

sentences.zh: 我欲遣一重臣往宣慰，便索春衣使，可乎？」

translations.literal: I wish to send a high minister to proclaim consolation and at once demand back the Spring Clothing envoy — would that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to send a senior minister to proclaim consolation and at once demand back the Spring Clothing envoy — would that be acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 度對曰：「克融家本兇族，無故又行淩悖，必將滅亡，陛下不足為慮。

translations.literal: Du replied: "Kerong's clan has always been a vicious one; without cause he has again acted in insolent defiance — he is bound for destruction, and Your Majesty need not worry overmuch.
translations.idiomatic: Du replied: "Kerong's clan has always been a vicious one. Without cause he has again acted in insolent defiance — he is bound for destruction, and Your Majesty need not worry overmuch.

sentences.zh: 譬如一豺虎，於山林間自吼自躍，但不以為事，則自無能為。

translations.literal: It is like a jackal or tiger roaring and leaping in the mountain forests — if one does not make an affair of it, it cannot achieve anything on its own.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a jackal or tiger roaring and leaping in the mountain forests — if one does not make an affair of it, it cannot achieve anything on its own.

sentences.zh: 此賊只敢於巢穴中無禮，動即不得。

translations.literal: This bandit only dares be discourteous within his lair; once he stirs, he will fail.
translations.idiomatic: This rebel only dares be insolent within his lair; the moment he stirs, he will fail.

sentences.zh: 今亦不須遣使宣慰，亦不要索所留敕使，但更緩旬日已來，與一詔云：『聞中官到彼稍失去就，待到，我當有處分。

translations.literal: Now there is no need to send an envoy to proclaim consolation, nor to demand back the detained imperial messenger. Just wait another ten days or so and issue an edict saying: 'We have heard that when the palace envoy reached you matters were somewhat unsettled; when he arrives I shall have measures to take.
translations.idiomatic: Now there is no need to send an envoy to proclaim consolation, nor to demand back the detained imperial messenger. Just wait another ten days or so and issue an edict saying: 'We have heard that when the palace envoy reached you matters were somewhat unsettled; when he arrives I shall take appropriate measures.

sentences.zh: 所賜卿春衣，有司制造不謹，我甚要知之，已令科處。』

translations.literal: As for the spring clothing granted to you — the officials who made them were not careful; I very much wish to know of this and have already ordered penalties.'
translations.idiomatic: As for the spring clothing granted to you, the officials who made them were careless; I very much wish to know of this and have already ordered penalties.'

sentences.zh: 所請丁匠五千人及兵馬赴東都，固是虛語。

translations.literal: As for the five thousand corvée laborers and troops requested to go to the Eastern Capital, these are plainly empty words.
translations.idiomatic: As for the five thousand corvée laborers and troops requested to go to the Eastern Capital, these are plainly empty words.

sentences.zh: 臣料賊中，必出不得，今欲直挫其奸意，即報云：『卿所請丁匠修宮闕，可速遣來，已敕魏博等道，令所在排比供擬。』

translations.literal: I expect that among the rebels they cannot produce them. Now if we wish to blunt their scheming directly, respond thus: 'The corvée laborers you requested for repairing the palaces — dispatch them at once; I have already ordered the circuits of Weibo and the rest to arrange supplies along the route.'
translations.idiomatic: I expect they cannot produce them among the rebels. If we wish to blunt their scheming directly, respond thus: 'The corvée laborers you requested for repairing the palaces — dispatch them at once. I have already ordered the circuits of Weibo and the rest to arrange supplies along the route.'

sentences.zh: 料得此詔，必章惶失計。

translations.literal: Once this edict reaches them, they will surely panic and lose their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Once this edict reaches them, they will surely panic and lose their plan.

sentences.zh: 若未能如此，猶示含容，則報云：『東都宮闕，所要修葺，事在有司，不假卿遣丁匠遠來。

translations.literal: If we cannot do that and still wish to show forbearance, then respond: 'Repairs to the Eastern Capital palaces are the business of the proper offices — there is no need for you to dispatch corvée laborers from afar.
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot do that and still wish to show forbearance, then respond: 'Repairs to the Eastern Capital palaces are the business of the proper offices — there is no need for you to dispatch corvée laborers from afar.

sentences.zh: 又所言三軍春衣，自是本道常事。

translations.literal: And the spring clothing for the three armies you mention is itself a routine matter for your circuit.
translations.idiomatic: And the spring clothing for the three armies you mention is itself a routine matter for your circuit.

sentences.zh: 比來朝廷或有事賜與，皆緣征發，須是優恩，若尋常則無此例。

translations.literal: In recent times when the court has made special grants, it has always been because of mobilizations — a mark of exceptional favor. Under ordinary circumstances there is no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times when the court has made special grants, it has always been because of mobilizations — a mark of exceptional favor. Under ordinary circumstances there is no such precedent.

sentences.zh: 我固不惜三二十萬端疋，只是事體不可獨與范陽。

translations.literal: I would not begrudge two or three hundred thousand rolls of cloth, but the matter simply cannot be handled by granting them to Fanyang alone.
translations.idiomatic: I would not begrudge two or three hundred thousand rolls of cloth, but the matter simply cannot be handled by granting them to Fanyang alone.

sentences.zh: 卿宜知悉。』

translations.literal: You should understand this.'
translations.idiomatic: You should understand this.'

sentences.zh: 只如此處分即得，陛下更不要介意。」

translations.literal: Handling it in just this way will suffice — Your Majesty need give it no further thought."
translations.idiomatic: Handling it in just this way will suffice — Your Majesty need give it no further thought."

sentences.zh: 上從之，遂進詔章，至皆如度所料。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, and when the edicts were forwarded, everything fell out as Du had predicted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and when the edicts were forwarded, everything fell out as Du had predicted.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，幽州殺克融並其二子。

translations.literal: Within ten days Youzhou killed Kerong along with his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Youzhou killed Kerong along with his two sons.

sentences.zh: 時帝童年驕縱，倦接群臣。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor, still young, was proud and self-indulgent, and had grown weary of receiving ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor, still young, was proud and self-indulgent and had grown weary of receiving his ministers.

sentences.zh: 度從容奏曰：「比者，陛下每月約六七度坐朝。

translations.literal: Du calmly memorialized: "Recently Your Majesty has held court roughly six or seven times each month.
translations.idiomatic: Du calmly memorialized: "Recently Your Majesty has held court roughly six or seven times each month.

sentences.zh: 天下人心，無不知陛下躬親庶政，乃至河北賊臣遠聞，亦皆聳聽。

translations.literal: Everyone in the empire knows that Your Majesty personally attends to everyday governance — even rebellious ministers far off in Hebei, hearing of it from afar, all listen with startled attention.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the empire knows that Your Majesty personally attends to everyday governance — even rebellious ministers far off in Hebei, hearing of it from afar, all listen with startled attention.

sentences.zh: 自兩月已來，入閣開延英稍稀，或恐大段公事須稟睿謀者，有所擁滯。

translations.literal: For the past two months, entering the inner hall and opening Yanying audiences has grown somewhat rare; I fear that major public business requiring Your Majesty's counsel may be piling up.
translations.idiomatic: For the past two months, entering the inner hall and opening Yanying audiences has grown somewhat rare. I fear that major public business requiring Your Majesty's counsel may be piling up.

sentences.zh: 伏冀陛下乘涼數坐，以廣延問。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will take advantage of the cool season to sit in audience more often and broaden the scope of deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will take advantage of the cool season to sit in audience more often and broaden the scope of deliberation.

sentences.zh: 伏以頤養聖躬，在於順適時候。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that nourishing the imperial person lies in harmonizing with the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that nourishing the imperial person lies in harmonizing with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 若飲食有節，寢興有常，四體唯和，萬壽可保。

translations.literal: If food and drink are regulated, sleep and rising fixed, and the four limbs kept in harmony, ten thousand years of life may be assured.
translations.idiomatic: If food and drink are regulated, sleep and rising fixed, and the four limbs kept in harmony, long life may be assured.

sentences.zh: 道書云：『春夏早起，取雞鳴時；

translations.literal: The Daoist texts say: 'In spring and summer rise early, at cockcrow;
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist texts say: 'In spring and summer rise early, at cockcrow;

sentences.zh: 秋冬晏起，取日出時。』

translations.literal: in autumn and winter rise late, at sunrise.'
translations.idiomatic: in autumn and winter rise late, at sunrise.'

sentences.zh: 蓋在陽則欲及陰涼，在陰則欲及溫暖。

translations.literal: This is because when yang prevails one seeks cool shade, and when yin prevails one seeks warmth.
translations.idiomatic: This is because when yang prevails one seeks cool shade, and when yin prevails one seeks warmth.

sentences.zh: 今陛下憂勤庶政，親覽萬機，每禦延英，召臣等奏對，方屬盛夏，宜在清晨。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty labors over everyday governance and personally reviews the myriad affairs of state. Whenever Your Majesty attends Yanying and summons us to respond, it is the height of summer — the hour should be early morning.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty labors over everyday governance and personally reviews the myriad affairs of state. Whenever Your Majesty attends Yanying and summons us to respond, it is the height of summer — the hour should be early morning.

sentences.zh: 如至巳午之間，即當炎赫之際，雖日昃忘食，不憚其勞，仰瞻扆旒，亦似煩熱。

translations.literal: If it reaches the hours between si and wu, that is the fiercest heat. Though Your Majesty toils until sunset forgetting meals and fears no fatigue, looking up at the imperial screen and tassels, one still seems oppressed by heat.
translations.idiomatic: If it reaches the hours between si and wu, that is the fiercest heat. Though Your Majesty toils until sunset forgetting meals and fears no fatigue, looking up at the imperial screen and tassels, one still seems oppressed by heat.

sentences.zh: 臣等已曾陳論，切望聽納。」

translations.literal: We have already stated this argument before and earnestly hope Your Majesty will heed it."
translations.idiomatic: We have already stated this argument before and earnestly hope Your Majesty will heed it."

sentences.zh: 自後，視事稍頻。

translations.literal: Thereafter the emperor attended to business somewhat more frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor attended to business somewhat more frequently.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼領度支。

translations.literal: Before long Du was additionally put in charge of the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Du was additionally put in charge of the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 屬盜起禁闈，宮車晏駕，度與中貴人密謀，誅劉克明等，迎江王立為天子。

translations.literal: When robbers rose within the Forbidden Quarter and the imperial carriage met its sudden end, Du secretly plotted with palace eunuchs, executed Liu Keming and the rest, and welcomed Prince Jiang to be enthroned as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers rose within the Forbidden Quarter and the imperial carriage met its sudden end, Du secretly plotted with palace eunuchs, executed Liu Keming and the rest, and welcomed Prince Jiang to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以功加門下侍郎、集賢殿大學士、太清宮使，余如故。

translations.literal: For his merit he was additionally made vice-director of the Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and commissioner of the Taiqing Palace; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was additionally made vice-director of the Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and commissioner of the Taiqing Palace; his other offices remained as before.

sentences.zh: 以贊導之勛，進階特進。

translations.literal: For his merit in guiding and supporting the enthronement, he was promoted in rank to specially advanced.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in guiding and supporting the enthronement, he was promoted in rank to specially advanced.

sentences.zh: 時滄景節度使李全略死，其子同捷竊弄兵柄，以求繼襲。

translations.literal: At this time Li Quanlue, military commissioner of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized control of the army in hopes of inheriting the post.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Quanlue, military commissioner of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized control of the army in hopes of inheriting the post.

sentences.zh: 度請行誅伐，逾年而同捷誅。

translations.literal: Du requested a punitive campaign; more than a year later Tongjie was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Du requested a punitive campaign; more than a year later Tongjie was executed.

sentences.zh: 因拜疏上陳調兵食非宰相事，請歸諸有司。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial stating that managing troops and provisions was not a chief minister's business and asking that these duties be returned to the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial stating that managing troops and provisions was not a chief minister's business and asking that these duties be returned to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 度年高多病，上疏懇辭機務，恩禮彌厚。

translations.literal: Du, advanced in years and often ill, submitted a memorial earnestly declining affairs of state; imperial favor and courtesy grew only the more generous.
translations.idiomatic: Du, advanced in years and often ill, submitted a memorial earnestly declining affairs of state; imperial favor and courtesy grew only the more generous.

sentences.zh: 文宗遣禦醫診視，日令中使撫問。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong sent imperial physicians to examine him and ordered palace envoys to inquire after him daily.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sent imperial physicians to examine him and ordered palace envoys to inquire after him daily.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，詔曰：昔漢以孔光降置幾之詔，晉以鄭沖申奉冊之命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, an edict stated: Formerly Han employed Kong Guang with an edict lowering the seat-furniture; Jin employed Zheng Chong to declare the investiture command.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, an edict stated: Formerly Han employed Kong Guang with an edict lowering the seat-furniture; Jin employed Zheng Chong to declare the investiture command.

sentences.zh: 雖優隆耆德，顯重元臣，而議政不及於咨詢，用禮止在於安逸。

translations.literal: Though honor and elevation were lavish for aged virtue and the chief minister was displayed as weighty, deliberation on government did not reach to consultation, and the use of rites stopped at ease and repose.
translations.idiomatic: Though honor and elevation were lavish for aged virtue and the chief minister was displayed as weighty, deliberation on government did not reach to consultation, and the use of rites stopped at ease and repose.

sentences.zh: 朕勤求至理，所寶唯賢，顧諟舊勞，敢不加敬。

translations.literal: We diligently seek the utmost principle and treasure only the worthy; looking upon old labor with reverence, how dare We fail to add respect?
translations.idiomatic: We diligently seek the utmost principle and treasure only the worthy; looking upon old labor with reverence, how dare We fail to add respect?

sentences.zh: 由是委宰制於大政，釋參決於繁務。

translations.literal: Therefore We entrust chief ministerial rule to great affairs and release joint deliberation from complicated duties.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We entrust chief ministerial rule to great affairs and release joint deliberation from complicated duties.

sentences.zh: 時因聽斷，誠望弼諧，遷秩上公，式是殊寵。

translations.literal: At times when We hear and decide matters, We truly hope for harmonizing assistance; elevating rank to the highest lord is this special favor.
translations.idiomatic: At times when We hear and decide matters, We truly hope for harmonizing assistance; elevating rank to the highest lord is this special favor.

sentences.zh: 特進、守司徒、兼門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，充集賢殿大學士、上柱國、晉國公、食邑三千戶、食實封三百戶裴度，稟河嶽之英靈，受乾坤之間氣；

translations.literal: Special Advancement, Acting Minister of Education, Concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Upper Pillar of the State, Duke of Jin, fief of three thousand households, actual enfeoffment of three hundred households — Pei Du — has received the spiritual brilliance of the river and mountains and the intervening qi of heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement, Acting Minister of Education, Concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Upper Pillar of the State, Duke of Jin, fief of three thousand households, actual enfeoffment of three hundred households — Pei Du — has received the spiritual brilliance of the river and mountains and the intervening qi of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 珪璋特達，城府洞開。

translations.literal: his jade and scepter are uniquely penetrating; his breast and countenance are open through and through.
translations.idiomatic: his jade and scepter are uniquely penetrating; his breast and countenance are open through and through.

sentences.zh: 外茂九功，內苞一德。

translations.literal: Outwardly he flourishes the nine achievements; inwardly he embraces the one virtue.
