translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he flourishes the nine achievements; inwardly he embraces the one virtue.

sentences.zh: 器為社稷之鎮，才實邦國之楨。

translations.literal: His vessel is the anchor of the altars of state; his talent is truly the pillar of the nation.
translations.idiomatic: His vessel is the anchor of the altars of state; his talent is truly the pillar of the nation.

sentences.zh: 故能祗事累朝，宣融景化。

translations.literal: Therefore he has reverently served successive reigns and spread and harmonized brilliant transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he has reverently served successive reigns and spread and harmonized brilliant transformation.

sentences.zh: 在憲宗時，掃滌區宇，爾則有出車殄寇之勛；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xianzong, sweeping and cleansing the realm — then you had the merit of going forth in chariots to exterminate bandits;
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Xianzong, sweeping and cleansing the realm — then you had the merit of going forth in chariots to exterminate bandits;

sentences.zh: 在穆宗時，混同文軌，爾則有參戎入輔之績；

translations.literal: in the time of Emperor Muzong, blending and unifying script and tracks — then you had the achievement of entering to assist after joining the army;
translations.idiomatic: in the time of Emperor Muzong, blending and unifying script and tracks — then you had the achievement of entering to assist after joining the army;

sentences.zh: 在敬宗時，阜康兆庶，爾則有活國庇人之勤。

translations.literal: in the time of Emperor Jingzong, enriching and bringing peace to the multitudes — then you had the diligence of saving the state and sheltering the people.
translations.idiomatic: in the time of Emperor Jingzong, enriching and bringing peace to the multitudes — then you had the diligence of saving the state and sheltering the people.

sentences.zh: 迨弼朕躬，總齊方夏，爾則有吊伐底寧之力。

translations.literal: When you came to assist Our person and gather together the regions of summer — then you had the strength of comforting the conquered and settling them at the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: When you came to assist Our person and gather together the regions of summer — then you had the strength of comforting the conquered and settling the realm.

sentences.zh: 皆不遺廟算，布在簡編，功利及人，不可悉數。

translations.literal: All without omitting the court's plans, spread in the bamboo slips and silk — benefiting the people and meriting achievement that cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: All without omitting the court's plans, spread in the bamboo slips and silk — benefiting the people and meriting achievement that cannot all be counted.

sentences.zh: 而朝論益重，我心實知。

translations.literal: Yet court opinion grows heavier, and in Our heart We truly know.
translations.idiomatic: Yet court opinion grows heavier, and in Our heart We truly know.

sentences.zh: 方用臯陶之謨，適值留侯之疾，瀝懇牢讓，備列奏章，塞詔上言，動形顏色。

translations.literal: Just as We were employing Gao Yao's counsels, it happened to coincide with Zhang Liang's illness — earnest plea and firm decline, fully listing memorial chapters; blocking the edict to report upward, moving the countenance in expression.
translations.idiomatic: Just as We were employing Gao Yao's counsels, it happened to coincide with Zhang Liang's illness — earnest plea and firm decline, fully listing memorial chapters; blocking the edict to report upward, moving the countenance in expression.

sentences.zh: 果聞勿藥之喜，更俟調鼎之功，而體力未和，音容尚阻。

translations.literal: We truly heard the joy of no need for medicine and awaited further the work of adjusting the cauldron — yet bodily strength is not yet harmonized and voice and countenance are still obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: We truly heard the joy of no need for medicine and awaited further the work of adjusting the cauldron — yet bodily strength is not yet harmonized and voice and countenance are still obstructed.

sentences.zh: 不有優崇之命，孰彰寵待之恩？

translations.literal: Without a command of lavish honor and elevation, who would display the grace of favored treatment?
translations.idiomatic: Without a command of lavish honor and elevation, who would display the grace of favored treatment?

sentences.zh: 宜其協贊機衡，弘敷教典；

translations.literal: It is fitting that you harmonize and assist the pivot and balance, broadly spread the teaching canon;
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting that you harmonize and assist the pivot and balance, broadly spread the teaching canon;

sentences.zh: 論道而儀刑卿士，宣德而鎮撫華夷。

translations.literal: discoursing on the Way to model the officials and spreading virtue to pacify and comfort Chinese and barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: discoursing on the Way to model the officials and spreading virtue to pacify and comfort Chinese and barbarians.

sentences.zh: 嗇養精神，保綏福履，為國元老，毗予一人。

translations.literal: Economize and nourish spirit, preserve and secure fortune and fulfillment — be the state's elder statesman and support Us alone.
translations.idiomatic: Economize and nourish spirit, preserve and secure fortune and fulfillment — be the state's elder statesman and support Us alone.

sentences.zh: 可司徒、平章軍國重事，待疾損日，每三日、五日一度入中書。

translations.literal: He is approved as Minister of Education and Grand Councilor for Military and State Affairs; when illness has diminished day by day, every three or five days once enter the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He is approved as Minister of Education and Grand Councilor for Military and State Affairs; when illness has diminished day by day, every three or five days once enter the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 散官勛封實封如故。

translations.literal: His honorary office, merit enfeoffment, and actual enfeoffment remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: His honorary office, merit enfeoffment, and actual enfeoffment remain as before.

sentences.zh: 仍備禮冊命。

translations.literal: Still prepare the rites and investiture command.
translations.idiomatic: Still prepare the rites and investiture command.

sentences.zh: 度表辭曰：「伏以公臺崇禮，典冊盛儀，庸臣當之，實謂忝越。

translations.literal: Du submitted a memorial declining: "I humbly observe that the elevated rites of the high offices and the grand ceremonies of investiture — for a mediocre servant to receive them is truly to exceed his desert.
translations.idiomatic: Du submitted a memorial declining: "I humbly observe that the elevated rites of the high offices and the grand ceremonies of investiture — for a mediocre servant to receive them is truly to exceed his desert.

sentences.zh: 況累承寵命，亦為便蕃，前後三度，已行此禮。

translations.literal: Moreover I have repeatedly received imperial favor, which has already grown frequent; three times already this ceremony has been performed for me.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have repeatedly received imperial favor, which has already grown frequent; three times already this ceremony has been performed for me.

sentences.zh: 令臣猶參樞近，竊懼無以弼諧，重此勞煩，有靦面目。

translations.literal: Now that I still serve near the pivot of power, I secretly fear I cannot harmonize and assist; to impose this labor again would leave me ashamed to show my face.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I still serve near the pivot of power, I secretly fear I cannot harmonize and assist; to impose this labor again would leave me ashamed to show my face.

sentences.zh: 伏乞天恩且課臣效官，責臣實事，冊命之儀，特賜停罷。

translations.literal: I humbly beg heavenly grace to set me only the test of performing my office and hold me accountable for real work — the ceremony of investiture, I pray, be specially suspended.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg heavenly grace to set me only the test of performing my office and hold me accountable for real work — the ceremony of investiture, I pray, be specially suspended.

sentences.zh: 則素餐高位，空負恥於中心；

translations.literal: Then though I occupy a high place while eating without merit, I would at least not bear shame in my heart;
translations.idiomatic: Then though I occupy a high place while eating without merit, I would at least not bear shame in my heart;

sentences.zh: 弁冕輕車，免譏誚於眾口。」

translations.literal: and though I wear the cap and carriage of rank, I would escape reproach from the crowd."
translations.idiomatic: and though I wear the cap and carriage of rank, I would escape reproach from the crowd."

sentences.zh: 優詔從之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 九月，加守司徒、兼侍中、襄州刺史，充山南東道節度觀察、臨漢監牧等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was additionally made acting Minister of Works, concurrently chief minister, prefect of Xiangzhou, and commissioner of the military governorship and inspection of Shannan East Circuit, commissioner of Linhan Pasturage, and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was additionally made acting Minister of Works, concurrently chief minister, prefect of Xiangzhou, and commissioner of the military governorship and inspection of Shannan East Circuit, commissioner of Linhan Pasturage, and related posts.

sentences.zh: 度素稱堅正，事上不回，故累為奸邪所排，幾至顛沛。

translations.literal: Du had long been known as upright and firm, unbending in service to his sovereign; therefore he was repeatedly ostracized by the wicked and nearly brought to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Du had long been known as upright and firm, unbending in service to his sovereign; therefore he was repeatedly ostracized by the wicked and nearly brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 及晚節，稍浮沈以避禍。

translations.literal: In his later years he yielded somewhat in stance to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he yielded somewhat in stance to avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 初，度支鹽鐵使王播，廣事進奉以希寵，度亦掇拾羨余以效播，士君子少之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Bo, commissioner of salt and iron in the Bureau of Revenue, had widely engaged in presenting tribute to court favor; Du also gathered surpluses to emulate Bo — men of principle thought little of this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Bo, commissioner of salt and iron in the Bureau of Revenue, had widely engaged in presenting tribute to court favor; Du also gathered surpluses to emulate Bo — men of principle thought little of this.

sentences.zh: 復引韋厚叔、南卓為補闕拾遺，俾彌縫結納，為目安之計。

translations.literal: He also brought in Wei Houshu and Nan Zhuo as remonstrance and review officials to patch connections and cultivate ties — a plan to keep his eyes at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought in Wei Houshu and Nan Zhuo as remonstrance and review officials to patch connections and cultivate ties — a plan to keep his eyes at ease.

sentences.zh: 而後進宰相李宗閔、牛僧孺等不悅其所為，故因度謝病罷相位，復出為襄陽節度。

translations.literal: Later chief ministers such as Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru disliked his conduct; therefore when Du pleaded illness and left the chief ministership, he was again sent out as military commissioner of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later chief ministers such as Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru disliked his conduct; therefore when Du pleaded illness and left the chief ministership, he was again sent out as military commissioner of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 初，元和十四年，於襄陽置臨漢監牧。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, Linhan Pasturage was established at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, Linhan Pasturage was established at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 廢百姓田四百頃，其牧馬三千二百余匹。

translations.literal: Four hundred qing of common people's fields were taken, and it pastured more than thirty-two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred qing of common people's fields were taken, and it pastured more than thirty-two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 度以牧馬數少，虛廢民田，奏罷之，除其使名。

translations.literal: Du, considering the number of horses too small to justify wasting people's fields, memorialized to abolish it and remove the commissioner's title.
translations.idiomatic: Du, considering the number of horses too small to justify wasting people's fields, memorialized to abolish it and remove the commissioner's title.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，以本官判東都尚書省事，充東都留守。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he assumed his existing rank to direct the Eastern Capital Secretariat and served as Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year he assumed his existing rank to direct the Eastern Capital Secretariat and served as Eastern Capital regent.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，進位中書令。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year he was promoted to chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year he was promoted to chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一月，誅李訓、王涯、賈餗、舒元輿等四宰相，其親屬門人從坐者數十百人；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the four chief ministers Li Xun, Wang Ya, Jia Su, and Shu Yuanyu were executed; relatives, disciples, and those implicated numbered in the dozens and hundreds;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the four chief ministers Li Xun, Wang Ya, Jia Su, and Shu Yuanyu were executed; relatives, disciples, and those implicated numbered in the dozens and hundreds;

sentences.zh: 下獄訊劾，欲加流竄。

translations.literal: they were thrown into prison for interrogation and slated for banishment.
translations.idiomatic: they were thrown into prison for interrogation and slated for banishment.

sentences.zh: 度上疏理之，全活者數十家。

translations.literal: Du submitted a memorial pleading for them, and several dozen families were entirely spared.
translations.idiomatic: Du submitted a memorial pleading for them, and several dozen families were entirely spared.

sentences.zh: 自是，中官用事，衣冠道喪。

translations.literal: From this time eunuchs held power and the way of scholars and officials was lost.
translations.idiomatic: From this time eunuchs held power and the way of scholars and officials was lost.

sentences.zh: 度以年及懸輿，王綱版蕩，不復以出處為意。

translations.literal: Du, his years reaching the age of hanging up the carriage, and with the royal norms in disarray, no longer cared whether he stayed in office or left it.
translations.idiomatic: Du, his years reaching the age of hanging up the carriage, and with the royal norms in disarray, no longer cared whether he stayed in office or left it.

sentences.zh: 東都立第於集賢裏，築山穿池，竹木叢萃，有風亭水榭，梯橋架閣，島嶼回環，極都城之勝概。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital he built a mansion in Jixian Lane, constructing hills and digging pools, bamboo and trees thickly clustered; there were breezy pavilions and waterside halls, ladder-bridges and raised walkways, islands winding about — the finest scenery in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Capital he built a mansion in Jixian Lane, constructing hills and digging pools, bamboo and trees thickly clustered; there were breezy pavilions and waterside halls, ladder-bridges and raised walkways, islands winding about — the finest scenery in the capital.

sentences.zh: 又於午橋創別墅，花木萬株；

translations.literal: He also created a villa at Wujiao Bridge with ten thousand plants and trees;
translations.idiomatic: He also created a villa at Wujiao Bridge with ten thousand plants and trees;

sentences.zh: 中起涼臺暑館，名曰「綠野堂」。

translations.literal: within he raised cool terraces and summer halls called the "Green Wild Hall."
translations.idiomatic: within he raised cool terraces and summer halls called the "Green Wild Hall."

sentences.zh: 引甘水貫其中，釃引脈分，映帶左右。

translations.literal: He drew Sweet Water through it, branching channels spreading left and right, gleaming on either side.
translations.idiomatic: He drew Sweet Water through it, branching channels spreading left and right, gleaming on either side.

sentences.zh: 度視事之隙，與詩人白居易、劉禹錫酣宴終日，高歌放言，以詩酒琴書自樂，當時名士，皆從之遊。

translations.literal: In the intervals of his official duties Du feasted all day with the poets Bai Juyi and Liu Yuxi, singing loudly and speaking freely, finding joy in poetry, wine, the zither, and books; eminent men of the time all joined his company.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of his official duties Du feasted all day with the poets Bai Juyi and Liu Yuxi, singing loudly and speaking freely, finding joy in poetry, wine, the zither, and books; eminent men of the time all joined his company.

sentences.zh: 每有人士自都還京，文宗必先問之曰：「卿見裴度否？」

translations.literal: Whenever someone returned from the Eastern Capital to the imperial capital, Emperor Wenzong would first ask him: "Have you seen Pei Du?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever someone returned from the Eastern Capital to the imperial capital, Emperor Wenzong would first ask him: "Have you seen Pei Du?"

sentences.zh: 上以其足疾，不便朝謁，而年未甚衰，開成二年五月，復以本官兼太原尹、北都留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: Because of his foot ailment, which made court audience inconvenient, yet his years were not greatly declined, in the fifth month of the second year of Kaicheng the emperor again added to his existing rank the posts of governor of Taiyuan, regent of the Northern Capital, and military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his foot ailment, which made court audience inconvenient, yet his years were not greatly declined, in the fifth month of the second year of Kaicheng the emperor again added to his existing rank the posts of governor of Taiyuan, regent of the Northern Capital, and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 詔出，度累表固辭老疾，不願更典兵權。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued Du repeatedly memorialized firmly declining on grounds of age and illness, unwilling to take up military authority again.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued Du repeatedly memorialized firmly declining on grounds of age and illness, unwilling to take up military authority again.

sentences.zh: 優詔不允。

translations.literal: A gracious edict refused to allow it.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 文宗遣吏部郎中盧弘往東都宣旨曰：「卿雖多病，年未甚老，為朕臥鎮北門可也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong sent Lu Hong of the Ministry of Personnel to the Eastern Capital to proclaim the imperial will: "Though you have many ailments, your years are not yet greatly advanced — you may lie in command of the Northern Gate for me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sent Lu Hong of the Ministry of Personnel to the Eastern Capital to proclaim the imperial will: "Though you have many ailments, your years are not yet greatly advanced — you may lie in command of the Northern Gate for me."

sentences.zh: 促令上路，度不獲已，之任。

translations.literal: He was urged to set out on the road; unable to refuse, Du took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was urged to set out on the road; unable to refuse, Du took up the post.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，病甚，乞還東都養病。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year his illness grew severe and he begged to return to the Eastern Capital to convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year his illness grew severe and he begged to return to the Eastern Capital to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，詔許還京，拜中書令。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year an edict permitted his return to the capital and appointed him chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year an edict permitted his return to the capital and appointed him chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以疾未任朝謝。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was unable to attend court to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was unable to attend court to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司徒、中書令度，綽有大勛，累居臺鼎。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Minister of Works and chief of the Secretariat Du has outstanding great merit and has repeatedly occupied the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Minister of Works and chief of the Secretariat Du has outstanding great merit and has repeatedly occupied the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 今以疾恙，未任謝上，其本官俸料，宜自計日支給。」

translations.literal: Now, owing to illness, he cannot perform the court thanks; the salary of his existing office should be paid from the day it is calculated."
translations.idiomatic: Now, owing to illness, he cannot perform the court thanks; the salary of his existing office should be paid from the day it is calculated."

sentences.zh: 又遣國醫就第診視。

translations.literal: Imperial physicians were also sent to his residence to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial physicians were also sent to his residence to examine him.

sentences.zh: 屬上巳曲江賜宴，群臣賦詩，度以疾不能赴。

translations.literal: At the time of the Shangsi Festival banquet granted at Qujiang, when ministers composed poems, Du could not attend because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the Shangsi Festival banquet granted at Qujiang, when ministers composed poems, Du could not attend because of illness.

sentences.zh: 文宗遣中使賜度詩曰：「註想待元老，識君恨不早。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong sent a palace envoy to bestow a poem on Du: "I fix my thoughts on awaiting the elder statesman — I regret not knowing you sooner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sent a palace envoy to bestow a poem on Du: "I fix my thoughts on awaiting the elder statesman — I regret not knowing you sooner.

sentences.zh: 我家柱石衰，憂來學丘禱。」

translations.literal: The pillar of my house is failing; in grief I resort to prayers like those of Qiu."
translations.idiomatic: The pillar of my house is failing; in grief I resort to prayers like those of Qiu."

sentences.zh: 仍賜禦劄曰：「朕詩集中欲得見卿唱和詩，故令示此。

translations.literal: He also bestowed an imperial note: "In my poetry collection I wish to see poems exchanged with you — therefore I show you this.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed an imperial note: "In my poetry collection I wish to see poems exchanged with you — therefore I show you this.

sentences.zh: 卿疾恙未痊，固無心力，但異日進來。

translations.literal: Your illness is not yet healed and you truly lack the strength of mind — but send them when you can on another day.
translations.idiomatic: Your illness is not yet healed and you truly lack the strength of mind — but send them when you can on another day.

sentences.zh: 春時俗說難於將攝，勉加調護，速就和平。

translations.literal: In spring, common wisdom says recovery is difficult — strive to tend yourself and quickly regain health.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, common wisdom says recovery is difficult — strive to tend yourself and quickly regain health.

sentences.zh: 千百胸懷，不具一二。

translations.literal: A thousand thoughts in my breast — I cannot set them all down.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand thoughts in my breast — I cannot set them all down.

sentences.zh: 藥物所須，無憚奏請之煩也。」

translations.literal: Whatever medicines you need, do not shrink from the trouble of memorializing for them."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever medicines you need, do not shrink from the trouble of memorializing for them."

sentences.zh: 禦劄及門，而度已薨，四年三月四日也。

translations.literal: When the imperial note reached his gate, Du had already died — on the fourth day of the third month of the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial note reached his gate, Du had already died — on the fourth day of the third month of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，震悼久之，重令繕寫，置之靈座。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was shaken and grieved for a long while; he ordered the note copied again and placed it upon the bier.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he was shaken and grieved for a long while; he ordered the note copied again and placed it upon the bier.

sentences.zh: 時年七十五，冊贈太傅，輟朝四日，赗賻加等。

translations.literal: At the time he was seventy-five; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor, court was suspended for four days, and funeral gifts were increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-five years old. The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor, suspended audiences for four days, and granted funeral gifts of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 詔京兆尹鄭復監護喪事，所須皆官給。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jingzhao prefect Zheng Fu to supervise the funeral; all needs were supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jingzhao prefect Zheng Fu to supervise the funeral, with all expenses borne by the state.

sentences.zh: 上怪度無遺表。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered that Du had left no death memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was surprised that Du had left no final memorial.

sentences.zh: 中使問之，家人進其稿草。

translations.literal: Palace envoys inquired; the family presented his draft.
translations.idiomatic: When palace envoys inquired, the family presented his draft.

sentences.zh: 其旨以未定儲貳為憂，言不及家事。

translations.literal: Its purport worried that the heir apparent was not yet settled and did not speak of household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Its substance expressed anxiety that the heir apparent had not yet been firmly established and said nothing of family matters.

sentences.zh: 度始自書生以辭策中科選，數年之間，翔泳清切。

translations.literal: Du began as a scholar, selected through literary policy examinations; within a few years he soared and swam in the clear and exalted ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Du had begun as a scholar, entering office through literary policy examinations, and within a few years had risen into the highest circles of court.

sentences.zh: 逢時艱否，而能奮命決策，橫身討賊，為中興宗臣。

translations.literal: Meeting times of hardship and adversity, he could rouse his life to decide policy, throw his body across to attack bandits, and become a founding minister of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When the times turned harsh he could stake his life on decisive action, throw himself into the suppression of rebels, and become a founding minister of the restoration.

sentences.zh: 當元和、長慶間，亂臣賊子，蓄銳喪氣，憚度之威稜。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe and Changqing periods, rebellious ministers and traitorous sons, though gathering sharpness, lost their spirit and feared Du's awl-edge authority.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe and Changqing reigns, rebellious ministers and traitorous sons, though they had gathered their strength, lost heart before Du's formidable authority.

sentences.zh: 度狀貌不逾中人，而風彩俊爽，占對雄辯，觀聽者為之聳然。

translations.literal: Du's appearance did not exceed that of an ordinary man, yet his bearing was handsome and bright; in audience he was boldly eloquent, and those who saw and heard him were startled upright.
translations.idiomatic: Du's appearance was no more than that of an ordinary man, yet his bearing was handsome and spirited, and in audience he spoke with bold eloquence that made all who heard him sit up straight.

sentences.zh: 時有奉使絕域者，四夷君長必問度之年齡幾何，狀貌孰似，天子用否？

translations.literal: At that time when envoys were sent to distant regions, the rulers of the four barbarians always asked Du's age, what his appearance resembled, and whether the Son of Heaven employed him?
translations.idiomatic: When envoys were sent to distant lands, the rulers of the frontier peoples invariably asked how old Du was, what he looked like, and whether the Son of Heaven still employed him?

sentences.zh: 其威名播於憬俗，為華夷畏服也如此。

translations.literal: His awesome name spread among distant peoples; that Chinese and barbarians alike feared and submitted to him was thus.
translations.idiomatic: His renown spread even among distant peoples, and Chinese and foreigners alike feared and respected him to this degree.

sentences.zh: 時威望德業，侔於郭子儀，出入中外，以身系國之安危、時之輕重者二十年。

translations.literal: At the time his prestige, virtue, and achievements matched Guo Ziyi; entering and leaving court and command, for twenty years his person bound the state's safety and danger and the times' weight and lightness.
translations.idiomatic: His prestige, virtue, and achievements rivaled those of Guo Ziyi, and for twenty years, moving between court and command, his person alone bore the weight of the empire's safety.

sentences.zh: 凡命將相，無賢不肖，皆推度為首，其為士君子愛重也如此。

translations.literal: Whenever generals and ministers were appointed, whether worthy or unworthy, all placed Du first; that gentlemen and scholars loved and esteemed him was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever generals and ministers were appointed, worthy or not, all ranked Du first; such was the esteem in which gentlemen and scholars held him.

sentences.zh: 雖江左王導、謝安坐鎮雅俗，而訏謨方略，度又過之。

translations.literal: Although Wang Dao and Xie An of the Jiang left sat to stabilize refined and vulgar society, in grand counsel and strategy Du surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wang Dao and Xie An of the Eastern Jin had stabilized court and countryside by their presence, in grand strategy and statecraft Du surpassed even them.

sentences.zh: 有子五人：識、譔、讓、諗、議。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Shi, Zhuan, Rang, Shen, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Shi, Zhuan, Rang, Shen, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 度子 識識以廕授官，累遷至通議大夫、檢校右散騎常侍、壽州刺史、本州團練使、上柱國、襲晉國公、食邑三千戶、實封一百五十戶，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: Du's son Shi, Shi entered office by hereditary privilege and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting right regular attendant of the cavalry, prefect of Shouzhou, regimental commissioner of that prefecture, pillar of state, inheritor of Duke of Jin, fief of three thousand households, actual enfeoffment of one hundred fifty households, granted purple gold fish bag.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Shi entered office by hereditary privilege and rose through repeated promotions to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting right regular attendant of the cavalry, prefect of Shouzhou and regimental commissioner of that prefecture, pillar of state, inheritor of the dukedom of Jin with a fief of three thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of one hundred fifty households, and was granted the purple-gold fish bag of high rank.

sentences.zh: 大中初，改潭州刺史、御史中丞，充河南都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong, he was changed to prefect of Tanzhou and vice censor-in-chief, and commissioned as regimental and observation commissioner of the Henan metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong reign he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou and vice censor-in-chief, serving as regimental and observation commissioner of the Henan metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 八年，加檢校戶部尚書、鳳翔尹、鳳翔隴右節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was additionally appointed acting minister of revenue, prefect of Fengxiang, and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was additionally appointed acting minister of revenue, prefect of Fengxiang, and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，本官移許州刺史、忠武軍節度、陳許觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, retaining his former titles, he was transferred to prefect of Xuzhou, military commissioner of the Zhongwu army, and observation commissioner of Chen and Xu, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to prefect of Xuzhou, military commissioner of the Zhongwu army, and observation commissioner of Chen and Xu while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 度子 譔譔，長慶元年登進士第。

translations.literal: Du's son Zhuan, Zhuan passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Zhuan passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Changqing.

sentences.zh: 度子 讓讓初任京光府參軍，太和中度鎮襄陽，奏乞讓從行。

translations.literal: Du's son Rang, Rang first served as aide in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture; in the Taihe period when Du garrisoned Xiangyang, he memorialized requesting that Rang accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Rang first served as an aide in the Jingzhao metropolitan administration; when Du was posted to Xiangyang in the Taihe period, he memorialized asking that Rang accompany him.

sentences.zh: 度子 諗諗，大中五年，自大中大夫檢校右散騎常侍、御史大夫、宣州刺史、宣歙觀察使、上柱國、河東男、食邑三百戶，賜紫金魚袋，入朝權知刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Du's son Shen, Shen—in the fifth year of Dazhong, from grand master of the court, acting right regular attendant of the cavalry, censor-in-chief, prefect of Xuanzhou, observation commissioner of Xuan and She, pillar of state, Baron of Hedong, fief of three hundred households, granted purple gold fish bag—entered court and was provisionally appointed vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Du's son Shen—in the fifth year of Dazhong, while serving as grand master of the court, acting right regular attendant of the cavalry, censor-in-chief, prefect of Xuanzhou, observation commissioner of Xuan and She, pillar of state, Baron of Hedong with a fief of three hundred households, and holder of the purple-gold fish bag—entered court and was provisionally appointed vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並列方鎮，時人榮之。

translations.literal: The brothers together held frontier commands; people of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers simultaneously held regional commands, to the admiration of their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：德宗懲建中之難，姑息籓臣，貞元季年，威令衰削。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Emperor Dezong, chastened by the hardship of Jianzhong, indulged the frontier ministers; in the late Zhenyuan years imperial authority and orders declined.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Emperor Dezong, chastened by the disasters of the Jianzhong era, indulged the frontier governors, and by the late Zhenyuan years imperial authority had waned.

sentences.zh: 章武皇帝誌據宿憤，廷訪嘉猷。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangwu harbored long-standing resentment and in court sought excellent plans.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangwu harbored long-standing grievances and sought excellent counsel in court.

sentences.zh: 始得杜邠公，用高崇文誅劉辟。

translations.literal: At first he obtained Duke Du of Bin and employed Gao Chongwen to execute Liu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: At first he obtained Duke Du of Bin and employed Gao Chongwen to execute Liu Pi.

sentences.zh: 中得武丞相，運籌訓戎，贊成睿斷。

translations.literal: Midway he obtained Chief Minister Wu, who planned campaigns and trained armies and assisted in forming the sage emperor's decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Midway he obtained Chief Minister Wu, who planned campaigns, trained armies, and helped shape the emperor's decisive policies.

sentences.zh: 終得裴晉公，耀武伸威，竟殄兩河宿盜。

translations.literal: Finally he obtained Duke Pei of Jin, who displayed martial prowess and extended authority and ultimately exterminated the long-standing bandits of the two He rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he obtained Duke Pei of Jin, who displayed martial prowess, extended imperial authority, and ultimately destroyed the long-standing rebels of the two He regions.

sentences.zh: 雄哉，章武之果斷也！

translations.literal: How heroic was Zhangwu's resolute decisiveness!
translations.idiomatic: How formidable was Emperor Zhangwu's resolute decisiveness!

sentences.zh: 晉公以書生素業，致位臺衡，逢進遘屯，扼腕兇醜，誓以身徇，不亦壯乎！

translations.literal: Duke of Jin, from a scholar's plain vocation, reached the balance of the terrace; meeting advance and encountering adversity, he clenched his wrist at vicious ugliness and vowed to offer his body—was it not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin rose from a scholar's humble calling to the highest office, and when fortune turned harsh he set his jaw against vicious rebels and vowed to stake his life on the cause—is this not magnificent!

sentences.zh: 夫人臣事君，唯忠與義。

translations.literal: For a minister serving his ruler, only loyalty and righteousness remain.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his sovereign, a minister has only loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 大則以訏謨排禍難，小則以讜正匡過失，內不慮身計，外不恤人言，古人所難也。

translations.literal: In great matters, using grand counsel to dispel calamity; in small matters, using candid rectitude to correct errors; within, not calculating for one's person; without, not caring for others' words—what ancients found difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In great affairs to dispel disaster through grand counsel, in small affairs to correct errors through candid remonstrance, within not calculating personal safety and without heeding others' talk—this is what the ancients found difficult.

sentences.zh: 晉公能之，誠社稷之良臣，股肱之賢相；

translations.literal: The Duke of Jin could do this—truly a fine minister of the altars of soil and grain, a worthy chief minister of the arms and legs;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin could do all this—truly a fine servant of the state and a worthy chief minister;

sentences.zh: 元和中興之力，公胡讓焉！

translations.literal: the force of the Yuanhe restoration—how could the duke yield this!
translations.idiomatic: as to the power behind the Yuanhe restoration, how could he yield precedence to any other!

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼嘆周室陵遲，齊桓霸翼，而有微管之論。

translations.literal: Formerly Confucius lamented the Zhou house's decline, Duke Huan of Qi's hegemonic wings, and had the discourse on the slight merit of Guan Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Confucius lamented the decline of the Zhou house and praised Duke Huan of Qi's hegemony with his remark on the modest merit of Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 嘗承宗、師道之濟惡也，奸人遍四海，刺客滿京師。

translations.literal: When Chengzong and Shidao aided evil, treacherous men filled the four seas and assassins filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong and Shidao abetted rebellion, traitors filled the empire and assassins thronged the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃至關吏禁兵，附賊陰計，議臣言未出口，刃已揕胸。

translations.literal: Even to the point that frontier clerks and forbidden troops attached to the bandits' secret plots—before remonstrating ministers' words left their mouths, blades had already pierced their chests.
translations.idiomatic: Even frontier officials and imperial guards joined the rebels' secret plots, and remonstrating ministers were stabbed in the chest before their words left their lips.

sentences.zh: 茍非死義之臣，孰肯橫身冒難，以輔天子者？

translations.literal: If not ministers who would die for righteousness, who would be willing to throw their bodies across difficulty to assist the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Had there not been ministers willing to die for righteousness, who would have thrown himself into such danger to support the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 茍裴令不用，元和之世則時運未可知也。

translations.literal: If Lord Pei had not been employed, in the Yuanhe era the fortune of the times would have been unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: Had Lord Pei not been employed, the outcome of the Yuanhe era would have been impossible to foresee.

sentences.zh: 臣所以明左衽之嘆，宣聖獎賢之深。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore clarifies the sigh of left-lapel peoples and proclaims how deeply the sage rewarded the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: This is why your servant sets forth the sigh of the uncivilized peoples and proclaims how deeply the sage rewarded worthy men.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：晉公伐叛，以身犯難。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Duke of Jin attacked rebellion and with his person encountered difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: The Duke of Jin campaigned against rebels and personally faced danger.

sentences.zh: 用之則治，舍之則亂。

translations.literal: Employ him and there is order; set him aside and there is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When he was employed the realm was governed; when he was set aside disorder followed.

sentences.zh: 公去巖廊，復失冀方。

translations.literal: When the duke left the cliff gallery, Jifang was again lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the duke left the halls of state, the Hebei region was lost again.

sentences.zh: 穎、植之謀，信為不臧。

translations.literal: The schemes of Xun and Zhu were truly not good.
translations.idiomatic: The schemes of Li Xun and Zheng Zhu were truly wicked.
